title.zh: 卷四 帝紀第四 文宣帝
title.raw: 卷四 帝紀第四 文宣帝 Volume 4 Annals 4: Emperor Wenxuan

sentences.zh: 顯祖文宣皇帝諱洋，字子進，高祖第二子，世宗之母弟。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu Wenxuan, taboo name Yang, style Zijin, was Gaozu's second son and Shizong's younger maternal brother.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan, temple name Xianzu of Northern Qi, bore the personal name Yang and the style Zijin. He was the second son of Gao Huan and the younger maternal brother of Gao Cheng.

sentences.zh: 后初孕，每夜有赤光照室，后私嘗怪之。

translations.literal: When the empress first conceived, every night red light filled the chamber; the empress privately found it strange.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Lou first conceived, every night red light filled the chamber; she privately found it strange.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖之歸尒朱榮，時經危亂，家徒壁立，后與親姻相對，共憂寒餒。

translations.literal: At first, when Gaozu went over to Erzhu Rong, the times were perilous and the household had nothing but bare walls; the empress and her kin sat facing one another, sharing fear of cold and hunger.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan first went over to Erzhu Rong, the realm was in turmoil and the household had nothing but bare walls; Empress Lou and her kin sat facing one another, sharing fear of cold and hunger.

sentences.zh: 帝時尚未能言，欻然應曰「得活」，太后及左右大驚而不敢言。

translations.literal: The Emperor was not yet able to speak, but suddenly answered "We will live"; the empress dowager and those beside her were greatly startled and dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang was not yet able to speak, but suddenly answered, "We will live." The empress and those beside her were greatly startled and dared not speak.

sentences.zh: 及長，黑色，大頰兌下，鱗身重踝。

translations.literal: When grown he was dark-skinned, with large cheeks and a long jaw; his body bore a scaly pattern and his ankles were heavy.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he was dark-skinned, with large cheeks and a heavy jaw; his body bore a scaly pattern and his ankles were thick.

sentences.zh: 不好戲弄，深沉有大度。

translations.literal: He did not care for play and horseplay; he was deep and possessed great breadth of mind.
translations.idiomatic: He cared little for play and horseplay; he was reserved and possessed great breadth of mind.

sentences.zh: 晉陽曾有沙門，乍愚乍智，時人不測，呼為阿禿師。

translations.literal: At Jinyang there was once a monk who seemed by turns foolish and wise; men could not fathom him and called him Master Atuo.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinyang there was once a monk who seemed by turns foolish and wise; men could not fathom him and called him Master Atuo.

sentences.zh: 帝曾與諸童共見之，歷問祿位，至帝，舉手再三指天而已，口無所言。

translations.literal: The Emperor once went with other boys to see him; the monk asked each man's destined rank in turn, and when it came to the Emperor he only raised his hand and pointed repeatedly at heaven, saying nothing with his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang once went with other boys to see him; the monk asked each boy's destined rank in turn, and when it came to Gao Yang he only raised his hand and pointed repeatedly at heaven, saying nothing.

sentences.zh: 見者異之。

translations.literal: Those who saw this thought it strange.
translations.idiomatic: Those who saw it thought it strange.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘗試觀諸子意識，各使治亂絲，帝獨抽刀斬之，曰：「亂者須斬。

translations.literal: Gaozu once tested his sons' dispositions, giving each a snarl of tangled silk to put in order; the Emperor alone drew a knife and cut it, saying: "What is tangled must be cut.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan once tested his sons' dispositions, giving each a snarl of tangled silk to put in order; Gao Yang alone drew a knife and cut it, saying, "What is tangled must be cut.

sentences.zh: 」高祖是之。

translations.literal: " Gaozu approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Huan approved of this.

sentences.zh: 又各配兵四出，而使甲騎偽攻之。

translations.literal: Again he gave each men-at-arms to lead out in four directions, and sent armored cavalry to feign attack.
translations.idiomatic: Again he gave each son troops to lead out in four directions and sent armored cavalry to feign attack.

sentences.zh: 世宗等怖撓，帝乃勒衆與彭樂敵，樂免胄言情，猶擒之以獻。

translations.literal: Shizong and the others were frightened and broke; the Emperor mustered his forces and fought Peng Yue as enemy, and though Peng removed his helmet and spoke from the heart, the Emperor still captured him and presented him as captive.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng and the others were frightened and broke; Gao Yang mustered his forces and fought Peng Yue as an enemy, and though Peng removed his helmet and spoke from the heart, Gao Yang still captured him and presented him as captive.

sentences.zh: 後從世宗行過遼陽山，獨見天門開，餘人無見者。

translations.literal: Later, following Shizong in passing Mount Liaoyang, he alone saw the Gate of Heaven open; no one else saw it.
translations.idiomatic: Later, following Gao Cheng in passing Mount Liaoyang, he alone saw the Gate of Heaven open; no one else saw it.

sentences.zh: 內雖明敏，貌若不足，世宗每嗤之，云：「此人亦得富貴，相法亦何由可解。

translations.literal: Inwardly he was keen and sharp, yet in appearance he seemed deficient; Shizong often sneered at him, saying: "This man too will come to wealth and rank — how is face-reading to be explained.
translations.idiomatic: Inwardly he was keen and sharp, yet in appearance he seemed deficient; Gao Cheng often sneered at him, saying, "This man too will come to wealth and rank — how is face-reading to be explained?

sentences.zh: 」唯高祖異之，謂薛琡曰：「此兒意識過吾。

translations.literal: " Only Gaozu regarded him differently and said to Xue Shu: "This boy's understanding surpasses mine.
translations.idiomatic: " Only Gao Huan regarded him differently and said to Xue Shu, "This boy's understanding surpasses mine.

sentences.zh: 」幼時師事范陽盧景裕，默識過人，景裕不能測也。

translations.literal: " In youth he studied under Lu Jingyu of Fanyang; his retentive memory surpassed others, and Jingyu could not fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: " In youth he studied under Lu Jingyu of Fanyang; his retentive memory surpassed others, and Jingyu could not fathom him.

sentences.zh: 天平二年，授散騎常侍、驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、左光祿大夫、太原郡開國公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianping he was given Regular Palace Attendant, General of the Flying Cavalry, Lord Equal to Three Imperator, Left Grand Master of Splendor, and Duke of Taiyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianping 2 (535) he received Regular Palace Attendant, General of the Flying Cavalry, Lord Equal to Three Imperator, Left Grand Master of Splendor, and the dukedom of Taiyuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 武定元年，加侍中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wuding he was given Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuding 1 (543) he was made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 二年，轉尚書左僕射、領軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and General of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and General of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 五年，授尚書令、中書監、京畿大都督。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was given Director of the Masters of Writing, Director of the Secretariat Supervisor, and Grand Commander of the Capital Region.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he received Director of the Masters of Writing, Director of the Secretariat Supervisor, and the grand command of the capital region.

sentences.zh: 武定七年八月，世宗遇害，事出倉卒，內外震駭。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the seventh year of Wuding, Shizong was murdered; the affair was sudden and within and without all were shaken.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Wuding 7 (549), Gao Cheng was murdered; the affair was sudden and within and without all were shaken.

sentences.zh: 帝神色不變，指麾部分，自臠斬群賊而漆其頭，徐宣言曰：「奴反，大將軍被傷，無大苦也。

translations.literal: The Emperor's expression did not change; he directed the ranks, personally cut up the band of rebels and lacquered their heads, and slowly proclaimed: "The slaves have rebelled; the Grand General is wounded — there is no great harm.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang's expression did not change; he directed the ranks, personally cut up the band of rebels and lacquered their heads, and slowly proclaimed, "The slaves have rebelled; the Grand General is wounded — there is no great harm.

sentences.zh: 」當時內外莫不驚異焉。

translations.literal: " At the time none within or without was not startled.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time none within or without was not startled.

sentences.zh: 乃赴晉陽，親總庶政，務從寬厚，事有不便者咸蠲省焉。

translations.literal: He then went to Jinyang, personally overseeing general government, striving for clemency; matters that were inconvenient were all exempted or reduced.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Jinyang, personally overseeing general government and striving for clemency; matters that were inconvenient were all exempted or reduced.

sentences.zh: 冬十月癸未朔，以咸陽王坦為太傅，潘相樂為司空。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, on the first day guimwei, Prince of Xianyang Tan was made Grand Tutor and Pan Xiangle was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on the first day guimwei, Prince of Xianyang Gao Tan was made Grand Tutor and Pan Xiangle was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 十一月戊午，吐谷渾國遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on wuwu day, the Tuyuhun state sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on wuwu day, the Tuyuhun state sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 梁齊州刺史茅靈斌、德州刺史劉領隊、南豫州刺史皇甫眘等並以州內屬。

translations.literal: Liang's Inspector of Qizhou Mao Lingbin, Inspector of Dezhou Liu Lingdui, and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou Huangfu Shen and others all submitted their provinces within.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's Qizhou Inspector Mao Lingbin, Dezhou Inspector Liu Lingdui, and Southern Yuzhou Inspector Huangfu Shen and others all submitted their provinces.

sentences.zh: 十二月己酉，以并州刺史彭樂為司徒，太保賀拔仁為并州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on jiyou day, Bing Inspector Peng Yue was made Minister of Education and Grand Tutor Helou Ren was made Bing Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiyou day, Bing Inspector Peng Yue was made Minister of Education and Grand Tutor Helou Ren was made Bing Inspector.

sentences.zh: 八年春正月庚申，梁楚州刺史宋安顧以州內屬。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the eighth year, on gengshen day, Liang's Inspector of Chuzhou Song Angu submitted his province within.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring in the eighth year, on gengshen day, Liang's Chuzhou Inspector Song Angu submitted his province.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，魏帝為世宗舉哀於東堂。

translations.literal: On xinyou day the Wei Emperor held mourning for Shizong in the Eastern Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou day the Eastern Wei emperor held mourning for Gao Cheng in the Eastern Hall.

sentences.zh: 梁定州刺史田聰能、洪州刺史張顯等以州內屬。

translations.literal: Liang's Inspector of Dingzhou Tian Congneng, Inspector of Hongzhou Zhang Xian, and others submitted their provinces within.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's Dingzhou Inspector Tian Congneng, Hongzhou Inspector Zhang Xian, and others submitted their provinces.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，魏詔進帝位使持節、丞相、都督中外諸軍事、錄尚書事、大行台、齊郡王，食邑一萬戶。

translations.literal: On wuchen day the Wei edict advanced the Emperor to Bearer of Credentials, Grand Chancellor, Commander-in-Chief of All Armies at Home and Abroad, Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing, Grand Mobile Headquarters, Prince of Qi Commandery, with a fief of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day the Eastern Wei emperor edicted that Gao Yang be advanced to Bearer of Credentials, Grand Chancellor, Commander-in-Chief of All Armies at Home and Abroad, Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing, Grand Mobile Headquarters, and Prince of Qi Commandery, with a fief of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，地豆于國遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: On jiaxu day the Didouyu state sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu day the Didouyu state sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 三月辛酉，又進封齊王，食冀州之渤海長樂安德武邑、瀛州之河間五郡，邑十萬戶。

translations.literal: In the third month, on xinyou day, he was further enfeoffed as Prince of Qi, with the five commanderies of Bohai, Changle, Ande, and Wuyi in Jizhou and Hejian in Yingzhou, a fief of one hundred thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on xinyou day, he was further enfeoffed as Prince of Qi, with the five commanderies of Bohai, Changle, Ande, and Wuyi in Jizhou and Hejian in Yingzhou — a fief of one hundred thousand households.

sentences.zh: 自居晉陽，寢室夜有光如晝。

translations.literal: From the time he dwelt at Jinyang, his sleeping chamber at night had light like day.
translations.idiomatic: From the time he dwelt at Jinyang, his sleeping chamber at night had light like day.

sentences.zh: 既為王，夢人以筆點己額。

translations.literal: Once he was made prince, he dreamed that a man with a brush dotted his forehead.
translations.idiomatic: Once he was made prince, he dreamed that a man with a brush dotted his forehead.

sentences.zh: 旦以告館客王曇哲曰：「吾其退乎？

translations.literal: At dawn he told his guest Wang Tanzhe: "Am I to withdraw?
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he told his guest Wang Tanzhe, "Am I to withdraw?

sentences.zh: 」曇哲再拜賀曰：「王上加點，便成主字，乃當進也。

translations.literal: " Tanzhe bowed twice and congratulated him: "When the character for 'prince' receives a dot, it becomes the character for 'lord' — you are to advance.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Tanzhe bowed twice and congratulated him, "When the character for 'prince' receives a dot, it becomes the character for 'lord' — you are to advance.

sentences.zh: 」夏五月辛亥，帝如鄴。

translations.literal: " In the fifth month of summer, on xinhai day, the Emperor went to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fifth month of summer, on xinhai day, Gao Yang went to Ye.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，進相國，總百揆，封冀州之渤海長樂安德武邑、瀛州之河間高陽章武、定州之中山常山博陵十郡，邑二十萬戶，加九錫，殊禮，齊王如故。

translations.literal: On jiayin day he was advanced to Grand Chancellor, oversaw all affairs of state, and enfeoffed with the ten commanderies of Bohai, Changle, Ande, and Wuyi in Jizhou, Hejian, Gaoyang, and Zhangwu in Yingzhou, and Zhongshan, Changshan, and Boling in Dingzhou, a fief of two hundred thousand households, with the Nine Bestowals and extraordinary honors, remaining Prince of Qi as before.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day he was advanced to Grand Chancellor, given charge of all affairs of state, and enfeoffed with the ten commanderies of Bohai, Changle, Ande, and Wuyi in Jizhou, Hejian, Gaoyang, and Zhangwu in Yingzhou, and Zhongshan, Changshan, and Boling in Dingzhou — a fief of two hundred thousand households — with the Nine Bestowals and extraordinary honors, remaining Prince of Qi as before.

sentences.zh: 魏帝遣兼太尉彭城王韶、司空潘相樂冊命曰：

translations.literal: The Wei Emperor sent Acting Grand Commandant Prince of Pengcheng Shao and Minister of Works Pan Xiangle to invest him with the edict, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Wei emperor sent Acting Grand Commandant Prince of Pengcheng Gao Shao and Minister of Works Pan Xiangle to invest him with the edict, saying:

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 敬聽朕命：夫惟天為大，列晷宿而垂象；

translations.literal: Attend and hear Our command: Heaven alone is great — it arrays the sun and stars and hangs forth signs;
translations.idiomatic: Attend and hear Our command: Heaven alone is great — it arrays the sun and stars and hangs forth signs;

sentences.zh: 謂地蓋厚，疏川嶽以阜物。

translations.literal: Earth is said to be thick — it opens rivers and mountains to enrich the myriad things.
translations.idiomatic: Earth is said to be thick — it opens rivers and mountains to enrich the myriad things.

sentences.zh: 所以四時代序，萬類駢羅，庶品得性，群形不夭。

translations.literal: Thus the four seasons succeed one another, the myriad kinds throng together, the common multitude find their nature, and every form is spared untimely death.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the four seasons succeed one another, the myriad kinds throng together, the common multitude find their nature, and every form is spared untimely death.

sentences.zh: 然則皇王統曆，深視高居，拱默垂衣，寄成師相，此則夏伯、殷尹竭其股肱，周成、漢昭無為而治。

translations.literal: Then the sovereign and king inherit the calendar, gaze deeply from on high, hold silence and let the robe hang, and entrust accomplishment to teacher and minister — thus the Earl of Xia and the Yin minister gave their utmost as arms and legs, and King Cheng of Zhou and Emperor Zhao of Han ruled through nonaction.
translations.idiomatic: Then the sovereign and king inherit the calendar, gaze deeply from on high, hold silence and let the robe hang, and entrust accomplishment to teacher and minister — thus the Earl of Xia and the Yin minister gave their utmost as arms and legs, and King Cheng of Zhou and Emperor Zhao of Han ruled through nonaction.

sentences.zh: 頃者天下多難，國命如旒，則我建國之業將墜於地。

translations.literal: Lately the realm has been full of hardship and the fate of the state hangs like a pendant — then Our founding enterprise was about to fall to earth.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the realm has been full of hardship and the fate of the state hangs like a pendant — then Our founding enterprise was about to fall to earth.

sentences.zh: 齊獻武王奮迅風雲，大濟艱危，爰翼朕躬，國為再造，經營庶土，以至勤憂。

translations.literal: Prince Xianwu of Qi rose swiftly amid wind and cloud, greatly rescued peril and crisis, supported Our person, and remade the state, managing the common soil to the point of utmost toil and care.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xianwu of Qi rose swiftly amid wind and cloud, greatly rescued peril and crisis, supported Our person, and remade the state, managing the common soil to the point of utmost toil and care.

sentences.zh: 及文襄承構，愈廣前業，康邦夷難，道格穹蒼。

translations.literal: When Wenxiang took up the structure, he broadened the former enterprise still further, settled the state and smoothed hardship, and his Way reached the azure vault.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Cheng took up the structure, he broadened the former enterprise still further, settled the state and smoothed hardship, and his Way reached the azure vault.

sentences.zh: 王縱德應期，千齡一出，惟幾惟深，乃神乃聖，大崇霸德，實廣相猷。

translations.literal: The Prince accumulates virtue and answers the age — once in a thousand generations; subtle in foresight, deep in counsel, divine in spirit and sage in holiness, he greatly exalts hegemonic virtue and truly broadens the minister's design.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince accumulates virtue and answers the age — once in a thousand generations; subtle in foresight, deep in counsel, divine in spirit and sage in holiness, he greatly exalts hegemonic virtue and truly broadens the minister's design.

sentences.zh: 雖冥功妙實，藐絕言象，標聲示迹，典禮宜宣。

translations.literal: Though hidden merit and subtle reality lie beyond words and images, to set forth fame and show the trace, ritual and canon ought to be proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Though hidden merit and subtle reality lie beyond words and images, to set forth fame and show the trace, ritual and canon ought to be proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 今申後命，其敬虛受。

translations.literal: Now We renew the later command — reverently receive it in emptiness.
translations.idiomatic: Now We renew the later command — reverently receive it in emptiness.

sentences.zh: 王摶風初舉，建旟上地，庇民立政，時雨滂流，下識廉恥，仁加水陸，移風易俗，自齊變魯，此王之功也。

translations.literal: When the Prince first raised the wind and planted his banner on the upper land, sheltering the people and establishing government, timely rain poured in torrents; those below knew shame and integrity, benevolence was added to land and water, customs were changed and manners transformed — from Qi to Lu — this is the Prince's merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince first raised the wind and planted his banner on the upper land, sheltering the people and establishing government, timely rain poured in torrents; those below knew shame and integrity, benevolence was added to land and water, customs were changed and manners transformed — from Qi to Lu — this is the Prince's merit.

sentences.zh: 仍攝天臺，總參戎律，策出若神，威行朔土，引弓竄跡，松塞無煙，此又王之功也。

translations.literal: Still he held the Celestial Terrace and took part in all military law; plans issued like a god and awe ran over the northern soil; bow drawn, the enemy fled and the pine frontier knew no smoke — this too is the Prince's merit.
translations.idiomatic: Still he held the Celestial Terrace and took part in all military law; plans issued like a god and awe ran over the northern soil; bow drawn, the enemy fled and the pine frontier knew no smoke — this too is the Prince's merit.

sentences.zh: 逮光統前緒，持衡匡合，華戎混一，風海調夷，日月光華，天地清晏，聲接響隨，無思不偃，此又王之功也。

translations.literal: He continued the former thread of light, held the balance and set right the realm; Chinese and barbarian were mixed into one, winds and seas were tuned and the barbarians settled; sun and moon shed their brilliance, heaven and earth were clear and tranquil; sound met echo and none who thought did not submit — this too is the Prince's merit.
translations.idiomatic: He continued the former thread of light, held the balance and set right the realm; Chinese and barbarian were mixed into one, winds and seas were tuned and the barbarians settled; sun and moon shed their brilliance, heaven and earth were clear and tranquil; sound met echo and none who thought did not submit — this too is the Prince's merit.

sentences.zh: 逖矣炎方，逋違正朔，懷文曜武，授略申規，淮楚連城，漼然桑落，此又王之功也。

translations.literal: Far off the fiery south, long in violation of the correct calendar, cherishing letters and displaying martial power, he handed down strategy and declared the rule; cities of Huai and Chu linked together fell like frost and mulberry leaves — this too is the Prince's merit.
translations.idiomatic: Far off the fiery south, long in violation of the correct calendar, cherishing letters and displaying martial power, he handed down strategy and declared the rule; cities of Huai and Chu linked together fell like frost and mulberry leaves — this too is the Prince's merit.

sentences.zh: 關、峴衿帶，跨躡蕭條，腸胃之地，嶽立鴟跱，偏師才指，渙同冰散，此又王之功也。

translations.literal: Guan and Xian were his girdle and sash; he strode over desolation; in the land that was the realm's belly, peaks stood and owls perched; a partial force had only to point and they melted like ice scattered — this too is the Prince's merit.
translations.idiomatic: Guan and Xian were his girdle and sash; he strode over desolation; in the land that was the realm's belly, peaks stood and owls perched; a partial force had only to point and they melted like ice scattered — this too is the Prince's merit.

sentences.zh: 晉熙之所，險薄江雷，迥隔聲教，迷方未改，命將鞠旅，覆其巢穴，威略風騰，傾懾南海，此又王之功也。

translations.literal: Where Jinxi lay, steep beside river and thunder, far separated from sound and teaching and lost in direction unchanged, he ordered generals to marshal troops, overturned their nests, and with martial prestige wind-swift overawed the southern sea — this too is the Prince's merit.
translations.idiomatic: Where Jinxi lay, steep beside river and thunder, far separated from sound and teaching and lost in direction unchanged, he ordered generals to marshal troops, overturned their nests, and with martial prestige wind-swift overawed the southern sea — this too is the Prince's merit.

sentences.zh: 群蠻跋扈，世絕南疆，搖盪邊垂，亟為塵梗，懷德畏威，向風請順，傾陬盡落，其至如雲，此又王之功也。

translations.literal: The many barbarians were overbearing, severed from the southern frontier for generations, shaking the border marches and repeatedly becoming dust and stubble; cherishing virtue and fearing awe, they turned to the wind and asked to submit; leaning corners all fell, arriving like clouds — this too is the Prince's merit.
translations.idiomatic: The many barbarians were overbearing, severed from the southern frontier for generations, shaking the border marches and repeatedly becoming dust and stubble; cherishing virtue and fearing awe, they turned to the wind and asked to submit; leaning corners all fell, arriving like clouds — this too is the Prince's merit.

sentences.zh: 胡人別種，延蔓山谷，酋渠萬族，廣袤千里，憑險不恭，恣其桀黠，有樂淳風，相攜叩款，粟帛之調，王府充積，此又王之功也。

translations.literal: Barbarians of another kind spread through mountain valleys; chieftains of ten thousand clans over a thousand li relied on peril and were not respectful, indulging their fierceness and cunning; delighting in pure custom, they came together bearing tribute, and grain and silk levies filled the princely storehouse — this too is the Prince's merit.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians of another kind spread through mountain valleys; chieftains of ten thousand clans over a thousand li relied on peril and were not respectful, indulging their fierceness and cunning; delighting in pure custom, they came together bearing tribute, and grain and silk levies filled the princely storehouse — this too is the Prince's merit.

sentences.zh: 茫茫涉海，世敵諸華，風行鳥逝，倏來忽往，既飲醇醪，附同膠漆，毛裘委仞，奇獸銜尾，此又王之功也。

translations.literal: Across the boundless sea, age-long foes of the many Chinese, wind-borne and bird-swift, coming suddenly and going suddenly — having drunk rich wine they clung like lacquer; fur coats piled by the ren, strange beasts led by the tail — this too is the Prince's merit.
translations.idiomatic: Across the boundless sea, age-long foes of the many Chinese, wind-borne and bird-swift, coming suddenly and going suddenly — having drunk rich wine they clung like lacquer; fur coats piled by the ren, strange beasts led by the tail — this too is the Prince's merit.

sentences.zh: 秦川尚阻，作我仇讎，爰挹椒蘭，飛書請好，天動其衷，辭卑禮厚，區宇乂甯，遐邇畢至，此又王之功也。

translations.literal: Qinchuan was still blocked, making itself Our foe; then they drew pepper and orchid and sent letters asking for friendship; heaven moved their inmost hearts, their words were humble and their rites thick; the realm was settled and quiet, far and near all arrived — this too is the Prince's merit.
translations.idiomatic: Qinchuan was still blocked, making itself Our foe; then they drew pepper and orchid and sent letters asking for friendship; heaven moved their inmost hearts, their words were humble and their rites thick; the realm was settled and quiet, far and near all arrived — this too is the Prince's merit.

sentences.zh: 江陰告禍，民無適歸，蕭宗子弟，尚相投庇，如鳥還山，猶川赴海，荊江十部，俄而獻割，乘此會也，將混朱方，此又王之功也。

translations.literal: The southern Yang reported calamity and the people had nowhere to turn; sons and younger brothers of the Xiao house still sought one another's shelter, like birds returning to mountains and streams running to the sea; ten districts of Jing and Jiang in a moment offered themselves cut away; seizing this occasion, he would mix Zhu and Fang — this too is the Prince's merit.
translations.idiomatic: The southern Yang reported calamity and the people had nowhere to turn; sons and younger brothers of the Xiao house still sought one another's shelter, like birds returning to mountains and streams running to the sea; ten districts of Jing and Jiang in a moment offered themselves cut away; seizing this occasion, he would mix Zhu and Fang — this too is the Prince's merit.

sentences.zh: 天平地成，率土咸茂，禎符顯見，史不停筆，既連百木，兼呈九尾，素過秦雀，蒼比周烏，此又王之功也。

translations.literal: Heaven level and earth complete, all under heaven flourishing; auspicious tokens appeared clearly and the scribes' brushes did not cease; connected trees numbered a hundred, and nine-tailed beasts appeared together; white surpassed the Qin sparrow, azure matched the Zhou crow — this too is the Prince's merit.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven level and earth complete, all under heaven flourishing; auspicious tokens appeared clearly and the scribes' brushes did not cease; connected trees numbered a hundred, and nine-tailed beasts appeared together; white surpassed the Qin sparrow, azure matched the Zhou crow — this too is the Prince's merit.

sentences.zh: 搜揚管庫，衣冠獲序，禮云樂云，銷沉俱振，輕徭徹賦，矜獄寬刑，大信外彰，深仁遠洽，此又王之功也。

translations.literal: He searched storehouses and promoted men of office; caps and robes received order; rites and music, long sunken, were both revived; light corvée and abolished levies, pity in prisons and lenient punishments, great faith shown abroad and deep benevolence reaching far — this too is the Prince's merit.
translations.idiomatic: He searched storehouses and promoted men of office; caps and robes received order; rites and music, long sunken, were both revived; light corvée and abolished levies, pity in prisons and lenient punishments, great faith shown abroad and deep benevolence reaching far — this too is the Prince's merit.

sentences.zh: 王有安日下之大勳，加以表光明之盛德，宣贊洪猷，以左右朕言。

translations.literal: The Prince has the great merit of settling the realm beneath the sun, and in addition displays the overflowing virtue of bright light; proclaim and assist the grand design, to stand at Our left and right in speech.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince has the great merit of settling the realm beneath the sun, and in addition displays the overflowing virtue of bright light; proclaim and assist the grand design, to stand at Our left and right in speech.

sentences.zh: 昔旦、奭外分，毛、畢入佐，出內之任，王宜總之。

translations.literal: In former times the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao were divided without, Mao and Bi entered to assist — the charge within and without the Prince ought to sum them.
translations.idiomatic: In former times the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao were divided without, Mao and Bi entered to assist — the charge within and without the Prince ought to sum them.

sentences.zh: 人謀鬼謀，兩儀協契，錫命之行，義申公道。

translations.literal: Human counsel and ghost counsel, the two principles in accord — the bestowal of command proceeds, righteousness declaring the public Way.
translations.idiomatic: Human counsel and ghost counsel, the two principles in accord — the bestowal of command proceeds, righteousness declaring the public Way.

sentences.zh: 以王踐律蹈禮，軌物蒼生，圓首安志，率心歸道，是以錫王大路、戎路各一，玄牡二駟。

translations.literal: Because the Prince treads law and steps in ritual, setting the standard for the myriad living, round heads rest in will and lead hearts return to the Way, therefore We bestow upon the Prince the Great Road and War Road, one each, with black stallions four-in-hand, two teams.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Prince treads law and steps in ritual, setting the standard for the myriad living, round heads rest in will and lead hearts return to the Way, therefore We bestow upon the Prince the Great Road and War Road, one each, with black stallions four-in-hand, two teams.

sentences.zh: 王深重民天，唯本是務，衣食之用，榮辱所由，是用錫王袞冕之服，赤舄副焉。

translations.literal: The Prince deeply weighs the people as heaven and takes the root as his task; clothing and food are the source of honor and disgrace — therefore We bestow upon the Prince the robe and cap of the nine emblems, with red slippers besides.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince deeply weighs the people as heaven and takes the root as his task; clothing and food are the source of honor and disgrace — therefore We bestow upon the Prince the robe and cap of the nine emblems, with red slippers besides.

sentences.zh: 王深廣惠和，易調風化，神祗且格，功德可象，是用錫王軒懸之樂，六佾之舞。

translations.literal: The Prince deeply broadens kindness and harmony, easily tunes wind and transformation; spirits and gods draw near and merit and virtue can be imaged — therefore We bestow upon the Prince suspended music and the dance of six rows.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince deeply broadens kindness and harmony, easily tunes wind and transformation; spirits and gods draw near and merit and virtue can be imaged — therefore We bestow upon the Prince suspended music and the dance of six rows.

sentences.zh: 王風聲振赫，九域咸綏，遠人率俾，奔走委贐，是用錫王朱戶以居。

translations.literal: The Prince's fame and sound shake brilliantly and the nine regions are all soothed; distant men lead and submit, running to present gifts — therefore We bestow upon the Prince vermilion doors to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince's fame and sound shake brilliantly and the nine regions are all soothed; distant men lead and submit, running to present gifts — therefore We bestow upon the Prince vermilion doors to dwell in.

sentences.zh: 王求賢選衆，草萊以盡，陳力就列，罔非其人，是用錫王納陛以登。

translations.literal: The Prince seeks the worthy and selects the multitude, exhausting the grass and thickets; presenting strength and taking rank, none are not the right men — therefore We bestow upon the Prince the ascending steps to mount.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince seeks the worthy and selects the multitude, exhausting the grass and thickets; presenting strength and taking rank, none are not the right men — therefore We bestow upon the Prince the ascending steps to mount.

sentences.zh: 王英圖猛概，抑揚千品，毅然之節，肅是非違，是用錫王武賁之士三百人。

translations.literal: The Prince's heroic design and fierce breadth restrain and raise a thousand kinds; resolute in season, correcting what is and is not — therefore We bestow upon the Prince three hundred martial guards.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince's heroic design and fierce breadth restrain and raise a thousand kinds; resolute in season, correcting what is and is not — therefore We bestow upon the Prince three hundred martial guards.

sentences.zh: 王興亡所繫，制極幽顯，糾行天討，罪人咸得，是用錫王鈇鉞各一。

translations.literal: The Prince is tied to rise and fall; he sets the utmost limit of dark and bright, corrects heaven's punishment, and the guilty all are taken — therefore We bestow upon the Prince axe and yue, one each.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince is tied to rise and fall; he sets the utmost limit of dark and bright, corrects heaven's punishment, and the guilty all are taken — therefore We bestow upon the Prince axe and yue, one each.

sentences.zh: 王鷹揚豹變，實扶下土，狼顧鴟張，罔不彈射，是用錫王彤弓一、彤矢百、盧弓十、盧矢千。

translations.literal: The Prince is hawk-soaring and leopard-changing, truly supporting the lower soil; wolf-looking and owl-spreading, none are not shot down — therefore We bestow upon the Prince one red bow, one hundred red arrows, ten black bows, and one thousand black arrows.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince is hawk-soaring and leopard-changing, truly supporting the lower soil; wolf-looking and owl-spreading, none are not shot down — therefore We bestow upon the Prince one red bow, one hundred red arrows, ten black bows, and one thousand black arrows.

sentences.zh: 王孝悌之至，通於神明，率民興行，感達區宇，是用錫王秬鬯一卣，珪瓚副焉。

translations.literal: The Prince's filial piety reaches utmost and passes through to the spirits; leading the people to rise and act, feeling reaches the regions — therefore We bestow upon the Prince one jar of black millet ale, with jade libation cup and ladle besides.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince's filial piety reaches utmost and passes through to the spirits; leading the people to rise and act, feeling reaches the regions — therefore We bestow upon the Prince one jar of black millet ale, with jade libation cup and ladle besides.

sentences.zh: 往欽哉。

translations.literal: Go — reverence!
translations.idiomatic: Go — reverence!

sentences.zh: 其祗順往冊，保弼皇家，用終爾休德，對揚我太祖之顯命。

translations.literal: Reverently follow the former register, preserve and assist the royal house, to the end employ your fine virtue, and respond to and raise Our Grand Ancestor's bright command.
translations.idiomatic: Reverently follow the former register, preserve and assist the royal house, to the end employ your fine virtue, and respond to and raise Our Grand Ancestor's bright command.

sentences.zh: 魏帝以天人之望有歸，丙辰，下詔曰：

translations.literal: Because the mandate of heaven and the people's hope had a place to return, on bingchen day the Wei Emperor issued an edict, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Because the mandate of heaven and the people's hope had a place to return, on bingchen day the Eastern Wei emperor issued an edict, saying:

sentences.zh: 三才剖判，百王代興，治天靜地，和神敬鬼，庇民造物，咸自靈符，非一人之大寶，實有道之神器。

translations.literal: The three powers were divided and distinguished, a hundred kings rose in succession, governing heaven and quieting earth, harmonizing spirits and revering ghosts, sheltering the people and creating things — all from numinous tokens; not one man's great treasure, but truly the sacred vessel of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: The three powers were divided and distinguished, a hundred kings rose in succession, governing heaven and quieting earth, harmonizing spirits and revering ghosts, sheltering the people and creating things — all from numinous tokens; not one man's great treasure, but truly the sacred vessel of the Way.

sentences.zh: 昔我宗祖應運，奄一區宇，歷聖重光，暨于九葉。

translations.literal: In former times Our clan ancestors answered the age and suddenly unified one region; sage after sage doubled the light, down to the ninth leaf.
translations.idiomatic: In former times Our clan ancestors answered the age and suddenly unified one region; sage after sage doubled the light, down to the ninth leaf.

sentences.zh: 德之不嗣，仍離屯圮，盜名字者遍於九服，擅制命者非止三公，主殺朝危，人神靡繫，天下之大，將非魏有。

translations.literal: Virtue did not continue; still we departed from peril and ruin; those who stole names filled the nine domains, those who usurped command were not limited to the Three Dukes; the lord was killed, the court endangered, human and divine had no tie — the great realm would no longer be Wei's.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue did not continue; still we departed from peril and ruin; those who stole names filled the nine domains, those who usurped command were not limited to the Three Dukes; the lord was killed, the court endangered, human and divine had no tie — the great realm would no longer be Wei's.

sentences.zh: 賴齊獻武王奮揚靈武，克剪多難，重懸日月，更綴參辰，廟以掃除，國由再造，鴻勳巨業，無德而稱。

translations.literal: We relied on Prince Xianwu of Qi to raise numinous martial power, cut down many hardships, rehung sun and moon, rejoined the Three Stars, swept the ancestral temple, and remade the state by the enterprise — a vast merit beyond words.
translations.idiomatic: We relied on Prince Xianwu of Qi to raise numinous martial power, cut down many hardships, rehung sun and moon, rejoined the Three Stars, swept the ancestral temple, and remade the state by the enterprise — a vast merit beyond words.

sentences.zh: 逮文襄承構，世業逾廣，邇安遠服，海內晏如，國命已康，生生得性。

translations.literal: When Wenxiang took up the structure, the enterprise grew still broader; near was soothed and far submitted, within the seas were tranquil; the fate of the state was already secure and the living found their nature.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Cheng took up the structure, the enterprise grew still broader; near was soothed and far submitted, within the seas were tranquil; the fate of the state was already secure and the living found their nature.

sentences.zh: 迄相國齊王，緯文經武，統茲大業，盡睿窮幾，研深測化，思隨冥運，智與神行，恩比春天，威同夏日，坦至心於萬物，被大道於八方，故百僚師師，朝無秕政，網疏澤洽，率土歸心。

translations.literal: Down to the Prince of Qi as Grand Chancellor, weaving letters and threading martial power, holding this great enterprise, exhausting wisdom and probing the subtle, studying the deep and measuring transformation — thought followed dark fortune, wisdom moved with the spirit; kindness matched spring heaven, awe matched summer sun; level heart reached the myriad things, the Great Way was spread to the eight directions; therefore the hundred officials were orderly, the court without bad government, the net sparse and the marsh rich, and all under heaven returned their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Down to the Prince of Qi as Grand Chancellor, weaving letters and threading martial power, holding this great enterprise, exhausting wisdom and probing the subtle, studying the deep and measuring transformation — thought followed dark fortune, wisdom moved with the spirit; kindness matched spring heaven, awe matched summer sun; level heart reached the myriad things, the Great Way was spread to the eight directions; therefore the hundred officials were orderly, the court without bad government, the net sparse and the marsh rich, and all under heaven returned their hearts.

sentences.zh: 外盡江淮，風靡屈膝，辟地懷人，百城奔走，關隴慕義而請好，瀚漠仰德而致誠。

translations.literal: Without, he exhausted the Yangtze and Huai; wind bowed and knees bent; opening land and cherishing men, a hundred cities ran; Guan and Long admired righteousness and asked for friendship; the boundless desert looked up to virtue and showed sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Without, he exhausted the Yangtze and Huai; wind bowed and knees bent; opening land and cherishing men, a hundred cities ran; Guan and Long admired righteousness and asked for friendship; the boundless desert looked up to virtue and showed sincerity.

sentences.zh: 伊所謂命世應期，實撫千載。

translations.literal: What is called a life answering the age truly comforts a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: What is called a life answering the age truly comforts a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 禎符雜遝，異物同途，謳頌填委，殊方一致，代終之迹斯表，人靈之契已合，天道不遠，我不獨知。

translations.literal: Auspicious tokens crowded in confusion, strange things on the same road; songs of praise piled up, different regions with one accord — the trace of dynastic end was already shown, the covenant of human and numinous already joined; heaven's Way is not far — We alone do not know.
translations.idiomatic: Auspicious tokens crowded in confusion, strange things on the same road; songs of praise piled up, different regions with one accord — the trace of dynastic end was already shown, the covenant of human and numinous already joined; heaven's Way is not far — We alone do not know.

sentences.zh: 朕入纂鴻休，將承世祀，籍援立之厚，延宗社之算，靜言大運，欣於避賢，遠惟唐、虞禪代之典，近想魏、晉揖讓之風，其可昧興替之禮，稽神祇之望？

translations.literal: We entered to receive the vast blessing and will inherit the age's sacrifice; relying on the thickness of established aid, extending the altar's span — speaking quietly of the great fortune, We rejoice in yielding to the worthy; far pondering the canon of abdication of Tang and Yu, near recalling the wind of bowing and yielding of Wei and Jin — how can We obscure the rites of rise and fall and examine the hope of spirits and gods?
translations.idiomatic: We entered to receive the vast blessing and will inherit the age's sacrifice; relying on the thickness of established aid, extending the altar's span — speaking quietly of the great fortune, We rejoice in yielding to the worthy; far pondering the canon of abdication of Tang and Yu, near recalling the wind of bowing and yielding of Wei and Jin — how can We obscure the rites of rise and fall and examine the hope of spirits and gods?

sentences.zh: 今便遜於別宮，歸帝位於齊國，推聖與能，眇符前軌。

translations.literal: Now We at once yield to the separate palace and return the imperial seat to the state of Qi, pushing the sage and giving ability, faintly matching the former track.
translations.idiomatic: Now We at once yield to the separate palace and return the imperial seat to the state of Qi, pushing the sage and giving ability, faintly matching the former track.

sentences.zh: 主者宣佈天下，以時施行。

translations.literal: The chief officer shall proclaim throughout the realm and implement it in season.
translations.idiomatic: The chief officer shall proclaim throughout the realm and implement it in season.

sentences.zh: 又使兼太尉彭城王韶、兼司空敬顯儁奉冊曰：

translations.literal: Again he sent Acting Grand Commandant Prince of Pengcheng Shao and Acting Minister of Works Jing Xianjun to present the register, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Again he sent Acting Grand Commandant Prince of Pengcheng Gao Shao and Acting Minister of Works Jing Xianjun to present the register, saying:

sentences.zh: 咨爾相國齊王：夫氣分形化，物繫君長，皇王遞興，人非一姓。

translations.literal: Consult you, Grand Chancellor Prince of Qi: Qi divided and forms transformed, things depend on a lord and elder; sovereign and king rise in turn — men are not of one surname.
translations.idiomatic: Consult you, Grand Chancellor Prince of Qi: Qi divided and forms transformed, things depend on a lord and elder; sovereign and king rise in turn — men are not of one surname.

sentences.zh: 昔放勳馭世，沉璧屬子；

translations.literal: In former times Yao governed the age and sank the jade disc, entrusting it to his son;
translations.idiomatic: In former times Yao governed the age and sank the jade disc, entrusting it to his son;

sentences.zh: 重華握曆，持衡擁璇。

translations.literal: Shun grasped the calendar, held the balance and embraced the jade pivot.
translations.idiomatic: Shun grasped the calendar, held the balance and embraced the jade pivot.

sentences.zh: 所以英賢茂實，昭晰千古，豈盛衰有運，興廢在時，知命不得不授，畏天不可不受。

translations.literal: Therefore heroic and worthy, abundant in reality, shone clearly through a thousand ages — how is it that flourishing and decline have a fortune, rise and fall lie in the time, knowing fate cannot but be granted, fearing heaven cannot but be received?
translations.idiomatic: Therefore heroic and worthy, abundant in reality, shone clearly through a thousand ages — how is it that flourishing and decline have a fortune, rise and fall lie in the time, knowing fate cannot but be granted, fearing heaven cannot but be received?

sentences.zh: 是故漢劉告否，當塗順民，曹歷不永，金行納禪，此皆重規襲矩，率由舊章者也。

translations.literal: Thus Han Liu reported ill fortune, Dangtu followed the people; Cao's calendar was not long, the Metal line received abdication — all these repeated the measure and followed the square, proceeding by the old canon.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Han Liu reported ill fortune, Dangtu followed the people; Cao's calendar was not long, the Metal line received abdication — all these repeated the measure and followed the square, proceeding by the old canon.

sentences.zh: 我祖宗光宅，混一萬宇。

translations.literal: Our clan ancestors illuminated the dwelling and unified the ten thousand realms.
translations.idiomatic: Our clan ancestors illuminated the dwelling and unified the ten thousand realms.

sentences.zh: 迄於正光之末，奸孽乘權，厥政多僻，九域離蕩。

translations.literal: Reaching the end of the Zhengguang era, wicked parasites seized power; that government was largely perverse, and the nine domains were torn apart.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Zhengguang era wicked men had seized power; government turned corrupt, and the realm was torn apart.

sentences.zh: 永安運窮，人靈殄瘁，羣逆滔天，割裂四海，國土臣民，行非魏有。

translations.literal: Yongan saw its mandate exhausted; men and spirits were destroyed and wasted; rebel hosts filled the sky, carving up the four seas—state and land, subjects and people, no longer seemed to belong to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongan the mandate ran out; men and spirits withered; rebels rose everywhere and carved up the empire—land and people no longer seemed Wei's own.

sentences.zh: 齊獻武王應期授手，鳳舉龍驤，舉廢極以立天，扶傾柱而鎮地，剪滅黎毒，匡我墜曆，有大德於魏室，被博利於蒼生。

translations.literal: Prince Xianwu of Qi seized the timely moment, rising like a phoenix and soaring like a dragon; he raised the fallen to establish Heaven, set propping pillars to steady the earth, cut down and extinguished the people's poison, righted our fallen calendar, bore great virtue toward the Wei house, and spread broad benefit upon the black-haired people.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xianwu of Qi took up the moment—rising like a phoenix, soaring like a dragon—raised the fallen throne, shored up the realm, uprooted the poison of chaos, and restored our broken calendar; great was his merit to Wei, wide his blessing to the people.

sentences.zh: 及文襄繼軌，誕光前業，內剿凶權，外摧侵叛，遐邇肅晏，功格上玄。

translations.literal: When Wenxiang succeeded the track, he brought forth light to the former enterprise: within he exterminated fierce power; without he shattered invading rebellion; far and near grew orderly and tranquil; his merit reached to High Dark Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxiang followed after, he carried the earlier work forward—crushing traitors within, breaking invaders without—until far and near grew quiet and his merit reached heaven.

sentences.zh: 王神祇協德，舟梁一世，體文昭武，追變窮微。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's spirit and the deities accord in virtue; you are boat and bridge for an age; your form is literary brilliance and martial display; you pursue change and exhaust the subtle.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's virtue aligns with heaven and earth; you are the bridge of an age, embodying civil splendor and martial might, probing change to its roots.

sentences.zh: 自舉跡藩旟，頌歌總集，入統機衡，風猷弘遠。

translations.literal: From your first footsteps at the frontier banner, songs of praise gathered all; entering to preside over the pivot-mechanism, your wind-teaching is vast and far.
translations.idiomatic: From your first days at the frontier banner, praise gathered everywhere; once you took the helm, your governance grew broad and far-reaching.

sentences.zh: 及大承世業，扶國昌家，相德日躋，霸風愈邈，威靈斯暢則荒遠賓士，聲略所播而鄰敵順款。

translations.literal: Having greatly inherited the worldly enterprise, upholding the state and prospering the family, your assisting virtue daily ascends; hegemonic wind grows ever loftier; when authority and spirit are thus unimpeded, the wild and distant come as guests; where renown and strategy spread, neighboring foes submit in good faith.
translations.idiomatic: Having inherited the great enterprise, you upheld the state and prospered the house—your virtue rising day by day, your hegemony spreading ever wider. Where your authority reaches, the distant come as guests; where your name travels, neighboring foes offer submission.

sentences.zh: 以富有之資，運英特之氣，顧盻之間，無思不服。

translations.literal: With the resource of wealth, wielding extraordinary spirit, in the blink of an eye none who think of it fail to submit.
translations.idiomatic: With boundless resources and a singular spirit, in a single glance none fail to submit.

sentences.zh: 圖諜潛蘊，千祀彰明，嘉禎幽秘，一朝紛委，以表代德之期，用啟興邦之迹，蒼蒼在上，照臨不遠。

translations.literal: Secret tokens lie hidden within; a thousand sacrifices make them clear; auspicious portents once dark and secret in one morning pour forth in array—to show the season for dynastic virtue, to open the track of rising state; Dark Dark Above gazes near, not far to shine upon.
translations.idiomatic: Hidden tokens long concealed now shine clear through a thousand rites; secret auspices pour forth in a single morning—to mark the hour when virtue changes hands and a new state rises. Heaven above looks down from no great distance.

sentences.zh: 朕以虛昧，猶未逡巡，靜言愧之，坐而待旦。

translations.literal: I, being empty and dim, still have not hesitated and withdrawn; quiet words bring shame; I sit awaiting dawn.
translations.idiomatic: I am unworthy and still have not withdrawn; even in silence I feel shame, sitting through the night until dawn.

sentences.zh: 且時來運往，媯舜不暇以當陽，世革命改，伯禹不容于北面，況於寡薄，而可踟躕。

translations.literal: Moreover when the time comes fate goes; Gui and Shun had no leisure to face south; when the world changed and the mandate turned, Bo Yu could not remain facing north—how much less one so meager and thin, who could dawdle!
translations.idiomatic: When the time comes, fate moves on—Emperors Gui and Shun could not linger on the throne; when the world changed, Yu could not remain in the north facing south. How much less can one as unworthy as I hesitate and delay!

sentences.zh: 是以仰協穹昊，俯從百姓，敬以帝位式授於王。

translations.literal: Therefore looking up to accord with vaulted Heaven, looking down to follow the hundred surnames, I reverently with formula confer the imperial seat upon Your Majesty the King.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I look up to heaven and down to the people, and solemnly confer the throne upon you, my king.

sentences.zh: 天祿永終，大命格矣。

translations.literal: Heaven's blessing ends forever; the great mandate has arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's blessing is at an end; the great mandate has passed.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 其祗承曆數，允執其中，對揚天休，斯年千萬，豈不盛歟！

translations.literal: Reverently receive the sequence of fate, truly hold the center, respond to and raise Heaven's favor—may this reign be ten thousand years—how could it not be glorious!
translations.idiomatic: Reverently accept the mandate, hold fast to the mean, and answer heaven's grace—may your reign endure ten thousand years! What glory could surpass this!

sentences.zh: 又致璽書於帝，遣兼太保彭城王韶、兼司空敬顯儁奉皇帝璽綬，禪代之禮一依唐虞、漢魏故事。

translations.literal: He also sent a seal-letter to the Emperor, dispatching Acting Grand Mentor Prince of Pengcheng Gao Shao and Acting Minister of Works Jing Xianjun to deliver the imperial seal and cord; the abdication rite followed entirely the precedents of Tang-Yao, Han, and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent a sealed letter to the emperor, dispatching Acting Grand Mentor Prince Pengcheng Gao Shao and Acting Minister of Works Jing Xianjun to present the imperial seal and cord; the abdication followed the ancient precedents of Yao, of Han, and of Wei.

sentences.zh: 又尚書令高隆之率百僚勸進。

translations.literal: Also Minister of Works Chief Gao Longzhi led the hundred officials in urging advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Chief Gao Longzhi also led the hundred officials in urging Gao Yang to accept the throne.

sentences.zh: 戊午，乃即皇帝位於南郊，升壇柴燎告天曰：

translations.literal: On wuwu, he thereupon ascended the imperial seat at the Southern Altar; mounting the altar with fagot-fire sacrifice he addressed Heaven, saying:
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Gao Yang ascended the throne at the Southern Altar; mounting the altar and kindling the sacrificial fire, he addressed Heaven:

sentences.zh: 皇帝臣洋敢用玄牡，昭告於皇皇后帝：否泰相沿，廢興迭用，至道無親，應運斯輔。

translations.literal: The Emperor, subject Yang, dares with black bull to clearly announce to August August Emperors and Empresses: adversity and ease follow in succession; abolition and rise alternate in use; the utmost Way is without partiality—when fate responds, one assists it.
translations.idiomatic: I, Yang, your subject, dare with a black bull to proclaim before the Lord on High and the Earth: fortune and ruin succeed each other; thrones rise and fall in turn; the Way shows no favor—it aids those whom fate chooses.

sentences.zh: 上覽唐、虞，下稽魏、晉，莫不先天揖讓，考歷終歸。

translations.literal: Looking up I examine Tang and Yu; looking down I trace Wei and Jin—none failed to first yield by bow in Heaven's command, examining the calendar until return was complete.
translations.idiomatic: From Yao and Shun above to Wei and Jin below, none failed to yield the throne when heaven decreed it, until the mandate ran its course.

sentences.zh: 魏氏多難，年將三十，孝昌已後，內外去之。

translations.literal: The Wei house had many troubles; the years nearly thirty; after Xiaochang, within and without abandoned it.
translations.idiomatic: Wei suffered calamity after calamity for nearly thirty years; after Xiaochang, court and realm alike turned from it.

sentences.zh: 世道橫流，蒼生塗炭。

translations.literal: The world's way flowed crosswise; the black-haired people were smeared on the roasting-block.
translations.idiomatic: The age ran wild; the people burned on the roasting-block of war.

sentences.zh: 賴我獻武，拯其將溺，三建元首，再立宗祧，掃絕羣凶，芟夷奸宄。

translations.literal: Relying on our Founding Wu, he rescued those about to drown; thrice he established chief heads, twice he re-established the ancestral temple; he swept away all villain bands and mowed down treacherous scoundrels.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to our Founding Ancestor, the drowning were pulled back—thrice he raised a ruler, twice he restored the ancestral line, sweeping away gangs of villains and cutting down traitors.

sentences.zh: 德被黔黎，勳光宇宙。

translations.literal: Virtue spread to black-headed masses; merit lit the universe.
translations.idiomatic: His virtue covered the people; his merit lit the universe.

sentences.zh: 文襄嗣武，克構鴻基，功浹寰宇，威陵海外，窮髮懷音，西寇納款，青丘保候，丹穴來庭，扶翼危機，重匡頹運，是則有大造於魏室也。

translations.literal: Wenxiang continued the martial track, able to construct the great foundation; merit soaked through the realm; authority overawed beyond the seas; those with hair to the roots held good faith; western bandits submitted; Blue Mound kept frontier guard; Cinnabar Cave came to court; he assisted at the crisis, again righted the falling fortune—this was great creation for the Wei house.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang followed in his footsteps and built the great foundation—merit filling the realm, authority reaching beyond the seas, distant lands keeping faith, western foes submitting, frontier tribes sending tribute. He steadied Wei in its crisis and righted its falling fortune—great indeed was his service to Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏帝以卜世告終，上靈厭德，欽若昊天，允歸大命，以禪於臣洋。

translations.literal: The Wei Emperor, because divination showed the era ending, Upper Spirits weary of virtue, reverently as to August Heaven, truly returned the great mandate, abdicating to subject Yang.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor, seeing that his dynasty's span was ending and heaven had turned from Wei, reverently acknowledged that the mandate belonged elsewhere and abdicated to me, Yang.

sentences.zh: 夫四海至公，天下為一，總民宰世，樹之以君，既川嶽啟符，人神效祉，群公卿士，八方兆庶，僉曰皇極乃顧於上，魏朝推進於下，天位不可以暫虛。

translations.literal: The four seas are utmost fairness; all under heaven are one; overseeing the people and governing the age requires setting a lord upon them—since rivers and mountains opened their tokens and men and spirits presented blessings, dukes, ministers, and gentry, the eight directions' myriad multitudes all say the imperial pole now looks above, and Wei pushes advancement below—the heavenly seat cannot for a moment stand empty.
translations.idiomatic: The four seas belong to all; the realm is one—ruling the people requires a sovereign. Rivers and mountains have shown their signs; men and spirits have blessed the change. Lords and ministers and the people of every land say heaven's gaze has turned upward while Wei yields from below—the throne cannot stand empty even for a day.

sentences.zh: 遂逼群議，恭膺大典。

translations.literal: Thus pressed by massed counsel, I reverently received the great ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed by the unanimous will of all, I reverently accept the great rite.

sentences.zh: 猥以寡薄，托於兆民之上，雖天威在顏，咫尺無遠，循躬自省，實懷祗惕。

translations.literal: Meanly with meager thinness, entrusted above the myriad multitudes—though Heaven's majesty is on my face and no distance within arm's reach, examining myself in reflection I truly harbor reverent fear.
translations.idiomatic: Unworthy as I am, I am placed above the people—though heaven's majesty is upon my brow and no distance is far from my reach, looking within myself I feel only reverence and dread.

sentences.zh: 敬簡元辰，升壇受禪，肆類上帝，以答萬國之心，永隆嘉祉，保祐有齊，以被於無窮之祚。

translations.literal: Reverently selecting the primordial day, mounting the altar to receive abdication, broadly classifying God Above, to answer the hearts of ten thousand states—forever elevating auspicious blessings, protecting and aiding You Qi, to extend to endless fortune.
translations.idiomatic: On this sacred day I mount the altar to receive the abdication and worship God above, to answer the hearts of all lands—may blessings flourish forever, may Qi be protected and its fortune extend without end.

sentences.zh: 是日，京師獲赤雀，獻於南郊。

translations.literal: That day the capital obtained a red sparrow and presented it at the Southern Altar.
translations.idiomatic: That day a red sparrow was caught in the capital and presented at the Southern Altar.

sentences.zh: 事畢，還宮，御太極前殿。

translations.literal: When the affair was done, he returned to the palace and held court at the Front Hall of Grand Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished, he returned to the palace and took his seat at the Front Hall of the Grand Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「無德而稱，代刑以禮，不言而信，先春後秋。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Having no virtue yet bearing the name, replacing punishment with rites; not speaking yet trusted, putting spring before autumn.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "To bear the name without merit is to govern by ritual rather than punishment; to win trust without words is to put nurture before severity.

sentences.zh: 故知惻隱之化，天人一揆，弘宥之道，今古同風。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that compassionate transformation makes Heaven and men one measure; the way of broad pardon is the same wind in ancient and modern times.
translations.idiomatic: Compassion links heaven and earth; mercy has been the same wind in every age.

sentences.zh: 朕以虛薄，功業無紀。

translations.literal: I, being empty and thin, have no record of achievement in merit-work.
translations.idiomatic: I am unworthy, my achievements without measure.

sentences.zh: 昔先獻武王值魏世不造，九鼎行出，乃驅御侯伯，大號燕、趙，拯厥顛墜，俾亡則存。

translations.literal: Formerly the Founding Xianwu Wang met Wei's unlucky times; the nine cauldrons wandered forth; he thereupon drove and commanded the feudal lords, raised the great name of Yan and Zhao, rescued their about-to-fall, causing the perished thus to exist.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei's evil hour our Founding Ancestor took up arms when the realm was lost, called the lords of Yan and Zhao to his banner, and snatched the falling dynasty from ruin, making the dead live again.

sentences.zh: 文襄王外挺武功，內資明德，纂戎先業，辟土服遠。

translations.literal: Prince Wenxiang outwardly thrust martial achievement, inwardly endowed with bright virtue; he inherited the martial track of the former enterprise, opened territory and brought the distant to submission.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wenxiang displayed martial prowess abroad and bright virtue at home, inheriting the martial enterprise and opening lands until distant peoples submitted.

sentences.zh: 年逾二紀，世歷兩都，獄訟有適，謳歌斯在。

translations.literal: Years passed more than two decades; generations crossed two capitals; prison lawsuits had their proper place; songs of praise were there.
translations.idiomatic: For more than twenty years, through two capitals, lawsuits were justly judged and songs of praise were heard.

sentences.zh: 故魏帝俯遵曆數，爰念褰裳，遠取唐、虞，終同脫屣。

translations.literal: Therefore the Wei Emperor bowed to follow the calendar sequence, thereupon thinking of lifting robe, far taking Tang and Yu, finally the same as casting off shoes.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor therefore bowed to heaven's decree, thinking to lift his robe and go—as Yao and Yu did before him—casting off the throne like an old shoe.

sentences.zh: 實幽憂未已，志在陽城，而群公卿士，誠守愈切，遂屬代終，居於民上，如涉深水，有眷終朝。

translations.literal: Truly hidden sorrow was not yet ended; his will was at Yangcheng—yet the massed dukes, ministers, and gentry, sincere in guardianship ever more pressing, thereupon entrusted the succession's end; dwelling above the people is like wading deep water, anxious through the whole morning.
translations.idiomatic: His heart still grieved and his wish was to withdraw to Yangcheng, but lords and ministers pressed ever more urgently; the mandate had passed and the throne could not stand empty. To reign over the people is to wade deep water—I feel that anxiety every morning.

sentences.zh: 始發晉陽，九尾呈瑞，外壇告天，赤雀效祉。

translations.literal: From first setting out from Jinyang, the nine-tailed fox presented auspice; at the outer altar heaven was addressed; the red sparrow showed blessing.
translations.idiomatic: From the day we set out from Jinyang, a nine-tailed fox appeared as an omen; at the altar we addressed heaven, and the red sparrow brought its blessing.

sentences.zh: 惟爾文武不貳心之臣，股肱爪牙之將，左右先王，克隆大業，永言誠節，共斯休祉。

translations.literal: You alone, civil and military ministers of undivided heart, arm-and-thigh and claw-and-tooth generals, who aided the former kings and jointly grandly built the great enterprise—forever speak sincere loyalty, together sharing this restful blessing.
translations.idiomatic: You civil and military ministers of loyal heart, you generals who were arm and claw to our former kings—you helped build this great work. May your loyalty endure, and may you share in these blessings.

sentences.zh: 思與億兆同始茲日，其大赦天下。

translations.literal: Thinking to with the hundred million begin together on this day—there shall be a grand amnesty throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On this day I would begin anew with all my people—a general amnesty is proclaimed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 改武定八年為天保元年。

translations.literal: Change Wuding year eight to Tianbao year one.
translations.idiomatic: Wuding year eight is changed to Tianbao year one.

sentences.zh: 其百官進階，男子賜爵，鰥寡六疾，義夫節婦，旌賞各有差。」

translations.literal: Officials shall advance in rank; men shall be granted nobility; widowers, widows, the six afflictions, righteous husbands and chaste wives—commendation and reward each with differences."
translations.idiomatic: Officials are promoted in rank; common men are granted nobility; widows, orphans, the disabled, worthy husbands and chaste wives—all are honored and rewarded according to merit."

sentences.zh: 己未，詔封魏帝為中山王，食邑萬戶﹔上書不稱臣，答不稱詔，載天子旌旗，行魏正朔，乘五時副車；

translations.literal: On jiwei, an edict enfeoffed the Wei Emperor as Prince of Zhongshan, fief of ten thousand households; in memorials he need not call himself subject, in replies no "edict" is used; he bears the Son of Heaven's banners, follows Wei's calendar, rides the five-seasons secondary carriage;
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei an edict enfeoffed the former Wei emperor as Prince of Zhongshan with a fief of ten thousand households; his memorials need not call him subject, nor would replies be styled as edicts; he would bear imperial banners, keep Wei's calendar, and ride the secondary chariot of the five seasons;

sentences.zh: 封王諸子為縣公，邑一千戶；

translations.literal: his sons were enfeoffed as district dukes, fiefs of a thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: his sons were enfeoffed as district dukes with fiefs of one thousand households;

sentences.zh: 奉絹萬匹，錢千萬，粟二萬石，奴婢二百人，水碾一具，田百頃，園一所。

translations.literal: he was granted ten thousand bolts of silk, ten million cash, twenty thousand piculs of grain, two hundred slaves, one water mill, a hundred qing of fields, and one garden estate.
translations.idiomatic: and he was granted ten thousand bolts of silk, ten million cash, twenty thousand piculs of grain, two hundred slaves, one water mill, a hundred qing of land, and an estate garden.

sentences.zh: 詔追尊皇祖文穆王為文穆皇帝，妣為文穆皇后，皇考獻武王為獻武皇帝，皇兄文襄王為文襄皇帝，祖宗之稱，付外速議以聞。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously honored the imperial grandfather Prince Wenmu as Emperor Wenmu, his consort as Empress Wenmu, the imperial father Prince Xianwu as Emperor Xianwu, the imperial elder brother Prince Wenxiang as Emperor Wenxiang; titles for the ancestors—entrust to outer offices for rapid deliberation and report.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously honored his grandfather as Emperor Wenmu and his grandmother as Empress Wenmu, his father as Emperor Xianwu, and his elder brother as Emperor Wenxiang; ancestral temple titles were referred to the outer offices for prompt deliberation and report.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，尊王太后為皇太后。

translations.literal: On xinyou, the Queen Mother was honored as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou the queen mother was honored as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，詔降魏朝封爵各有差。

translations.literal: On yichou, an edict lowered Wei-dynasty enfeoffments and ranks, each with differences.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou an edict reduced the titles and ranks of the former Wei court, each according to rank.

sentences.zh: 其信都從義及宣力霸朝者，及西來人並武定六年以來南來投化者，不在降限。

translations.literal: Those of Xindu who followed righteousness and those who declared strength for the hegemonic court, and those who came from the west, and all who since Wuding year six came south to submit and transform—are not within the reduction limit.
translations.idiomatic: Those of Xindu who had kept faith, those who had served the Gao cause, arrivals from the west, and all who since Wuding year six had come south to submit were exempt from the reduction.

sentences.zh: 辛未，遣大使于四方，觀察風俗，問民疾苦，嚴勒長吏，厲以廉平，興利除害，務存安靜。

translations.literal: On xinwei, envoys were dispatched to the four directions to observe customs, inquire into people's hardships, strictly admonish district officials, urge them with integrity and fairness, promote benefit and remove harm, striving to preserve tranquility.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei he sent envoys to every quarter to observe local customs, inquire into the people's hardships, and strictly admonish officials to govern with integrity, promote what benefits the people, remove what harms them, and keep the realm at peace.

sentences.zh: 若法有不便於時，政有未盡於事者，具條得失，還以聞奏。

translations.literal: If law has what is inconvenient to the time, or government has what is not exhaustive for affairs, fully itemize gain and loss and return to the capital to report.
translations.idiomatic: Where laws no longer fit the times or policies fall short, they were to itemize strengths and flaws and report back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，遷神主於太廟。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, the spirit tablets were moved to the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu the ancestral tablets were moved to the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 六月己卯，高麗遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: On jimao of the sixth month, Goguryeo sent envoys in court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao of the sixth month, Goguryeo sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，詔曰：「頃者風俗流宕，浮競日滋，家有吉凶，務求勝異。

translations.literal: On xinsi, an edict said: "Recently customs drift and float; vain rivalry daily grows; when families have fortune or misfortune, they strive to outdo in strangeness.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi an edict said: "Customs have grown loose and rivalry extravagant; in weddings and funerals every household strives to outdo the rest.

sentences.zh: 婚姻喪葬之費，車服飲食之華，動竭歲資，以營日富。

translations.literal: Expenses for marriage and funeral, splendor of carriage-robes, drink, and food—moving to exhaust a year's resources to scheme for daily wealth.
translations.idiomatic: The cost of marriages and funerals, the finery of carriage and dress, the luxury of food and wine—yearly income is poured out to flaunt daily wealth.

sentences.zh: 又奴僕帶金玉，婢妾衣羅綺，始以創出為奇，後以過前為麗，上下貴賤，無復等差。

translations.literal: Moreover slaves wore gold and jade; maidservants wore gauze and brocade—at first taking innovation as marvel, later taking surpassing predecessors as beauty; high and low, noble and base, again had no gradation of difference.
translations.idiomatic: Slaves wear gold and jade; maidservants wear silk and brocade—first novelty became fashion, then surpassing the last became the rule, until high and low knew no distinction.

sentences.zh: 今運屬惟新，思蠲往弊，反朴還淳，納民軌物。

translations.literal: Now fate belongs to renewal alone; thinking to wipe away former abuses, returning to simplicity and restoring purity, bringing the people within compass and things.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the mandate is renewed, we would wipe away old abuses, restore simplicity, and bring the people back within proper bounds.

sentences.zh: 可量事具立條式，使儉而獲中。

translations.literal: According to circumstances fully establish articles and forms, making thrift yet obtain the mean.
translations.idiomatic: Let regulations be drawn up as the times require, so that thrift may hold the mean."

sentences.zh: 」又詔封崇聖侯邑一百戶，以奉孔子之祀，並下魯郡以時修治廟宇，務盡褒崇之至。

translations.literal: Also an edict enfeoffed Lord Honored Sage with a fief of a hundred households to maintain sacrifice to Confucius, and ordered Lu Commandery timely to repair and maintain temple halls, striving to exhaust utmost praise and honor.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict enfeoffed Lord Honored Sage with a fief of one hundred households to maintain sacrifices to Confucius, and ordered Lu Commandery to repair the temple in due season with all due reverence.

sentences.zh: 詔分遣使人致祭於五嶽四瀆，其堯祠舜廟，下及孔父、老君等載於祀典者，咸秩罔遺。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched envoys separately to perform sacrifice at the Five Peaks and Four Rivers; the shrines of Yao and temples of Shun, down to Kong Fu, Lord Lao, and others recorded in the sacrificial canon—all received rites without omission.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were sent to offer sacrifice at the Five Sacred Peaks and Four Rivers; shrines to Yao and Shun, Kong Fu, Lord Lao, and all others in the sacrificial canon received rites without omission.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「冀州之渤海、長樂二郡，先帝始封之國，義旗初起之地。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The two commanderies of Bohai and Changle in Ji Province were the Former Emperor's first enfeoffment, the place where the righteousness-banner first rose.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "The commanderies of Bohai and Changle in Ji Province were our Founding Ancestor's first fief and the place where the banner of revolt first rose.

sentences.zh: 并州之太原、青州之齊郡，霸業所在，王命是基。

translations.literal: Taiyuan in Bing Province and Qi Commandery in Qing Province—where the hegemonic enterprise dwelt, where the kingly mandate was foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan in Bing Province and Qi Commandery in Qing Province were the seat of our enterprise and the foundation of our mandate.

sentences.zh: 君子有作，貴不忘本，思申恩洽，蠲復田租。

translations.literal: When a gentleman has accomplishment, he honors not forgetting roots; thinking to extend grace and reach, remission and restoration of land tax.
translations.idiomatic: A worthy man, when he achieves, does not forget his roots; thinking to extend grace to the land, we remit the land tax.

sentences.zh: 齊郡、渤海可並復一年，長樂復二年，太原復三年。」

translations.literal: Qi Commandery and Bohai may together be remitted one year; Changle remitted two years; Taiyuan remitted three years."
translations.idiomatic: Qi and Bohai are remitted one year, Changle two years, Taiyuan three years."

sentences.zh: 詔故太傅孫騰、故太保尉景、故大司馬婁昭、故司徒高昂、故尚書左僕射慕容紹宗、故領軍万俟干、故定州刺史段榮、故御史中尉劉貴、故御史中尉竇泰、故殷州刺史劉豐、故濟州刺史蔡俊等並左右先帝，經贊皇基，或不幸早徂，或殞身王事，可遣使者就墓致祭，並撫問妻子，慰逮存亡。

translations.literal: An edict: Former Grand Tutor Sun Teng, Former Grand Mentor Wei Jing, Former Grand Marshal Lou Zhao, Former Minister of Works Gao Ang, Former Left Vice Minister of Works Murong Shaozong, Former Army Commander Wanqigan, Former Inspector of Dingzhou Duan Rong, Former Palace Censor Liu Gui, Former Palace Censor Dou Tai, Former Inspector of Yinzhou Liu Feng, Former Inspector of Jizhou Cai Jun and others—all aided the former emperors and managed the imperial foundation; some unfortunately died early, some perished in royal service—envoys may be sent to their tombs to perform sacrifice, and also comfort and inquire after wives and children, extending solace to the living and the dead.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered sacrifice at the tombs of the late Sun Teng, Wei Jing, Lou Zhao, Gao Ang, Murong Shaozong, Wanqigan, Duan Rong, Liu Gui, Dou Tai, Liu Feng, Cai Jun, and others who had served the former emperors and built the dynasty—some dying early, some falling in the state's service—and directed that their wives and children be comforted, extending solace to living and dead.

sentences.zh: 又詔封宗室高岳為清河王，高隆之為平原王，高歸彥為平秦王，高思宗為上洛王，高長弼為廣武王，高普為武興王，高子瑗為平昌王，高顯國為襄樂王，高睿為趙郡王，高孝緒為脩城王。

translations.literal: Also an edict enfeoffed clan members Gao Yue as Prince of Qinghe, Gao Longzhi as Prince of Pingyuan, Gao Guiyan as Prince of Pingqin, Gao Sizong as Prince of Shangluo, Gao Changbi as Prince of Guangwu, Gao Pu as Prince of Wuxing, Gao Ziyuan as Prince of Pingchang, Gao Xianguo as Prince of Xiangle, Gao Rui as Prince of Zhaojun, Gao Xiaoxu as Prince of Xiucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict enfeoffed Gao Yue as Prince of Qinghe, Gao Longzhi as Prince of Pingyuan, Gao Guiyan as Prince of Pingqin, Gao Sizong as Prince of Shangluo, Gao Changbi as Prince of Guangwu, Gao Pu as Prince of Wuxing, Gao Ziyuan as Prince of Pingchang, Gao Xianguo as Prince of Xiangle, Gao Rui as Prince of Zhaojun, and Gao Xiaoxu as Prince of Xiucheng.

sentences.zh: 又詔封功臣厙狄干為章武王，斛律金為咸陽王，賀拔仁為安定王，韓軌為安德王，可朱渾道元為扶風王，彭樂為陳留王，潘相樂為河東王。

translations.literal: Also an edict enfeoffed meritorious ministers Kudi Gan as Prince of Zhangwu, Helü Jin as Prince of Xianyang, Heba Ren as Prince of Anding, Han Gui as Prince of Ande, Kezhuhun Daoyuan as Prince of Fufeng, Peng Yue as Prince of Chenliu, Pan Xiangle as Prince of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious ministers were enfeoffed: Kudi Gan as Prince of Zhangwu, Helü Jin as Prince of Xianyang, Heba Ren as Prince of Anding, Han Gui as Prince of Ande, Kezhuhun Daoyuan as Prince of Fufeng, Peng Yue as Prince of Chenliu, and Pan Xiangle as Prince of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 癸未，詔封諸弟青州刺史浚為永安王，尚書左僕射淹為平陽王，定州刺史浟為彭城王，儀同三司演為常山王，冀州刺史渙為上黨王，儀同三司淯為襄城王，儀同三司湛為長廣王，湝為任城王，湜為高陽王，濟為博陵王，凝為新平王，潤為馮翊王，洽為漢陽王。

translations.literal: On guim wei, an edict enfeoffed younger brothers: Qingzhou Inspector Gao Jun as Prince of Yong'an, Left Vice Minister Gao Yan as Prince of Pingyang, Dingzhou Inspector Gao You as Prince of Pengcheng, Opening-Fu Third Rank Gao Yan as Prince of Changshan, Jizhou Inspector Gao Huan as Prince of Shangdang, Opening-Fu Third Rank Gao Yu as Prince of Xiangcheng, Opening-Fu Third Rank Gao Zhan as Prince of Ch'angguang, Gao Jie as Prince of Rencheng, Gao Shi as Prince of Gaoyang, Gao Ji as Prince of Boling, Gao Ning as Prince of Xinping, Gao Run as Prince of Fengyi, Gao Qia as Prince of Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: On guim wei younger brothers were enfeoffed: Gao Jun, Qingzhou inspector, as Prince of Yong'an; Gao Yan, Left Vice Minister, as Prince of Pingyang; Gao You, Dingzhou inspector, as Prince of Pengcheng; Gao Yan, Opening-Fu Third Rank, as Prince of Changshan; Gao Huan, Jizhou inspector, as Prince of Shangdang; Gao Yu as Prince of Xiangcheng; Gao Zhan as Prince of Ch'angguang; Gao Jie as Prince of Rencheng; Gao Shi as Prince of Gaoyang; Gao Ji as Prince of Boling; Gao Ning as Prince of Xinping; Gao Run as Prince of Fengyi; and Gao Qia as Prince of Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，詔立王子殷為皇太子，王后李氏為皇后。

translations.literal: On dinghai, an edict established Prince Yin as Crown Prince, Queen Li as Empress.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai an edict established Prince Yin as crown prince and Lady Li as empress.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，詔乙太師厙狄干為太宰，司徒彭樂為太尉，司空潘相樂為司徒，開府儀同三司司馬子如為司空。

translations.literal: On gengyin, an edict appointed Grand Preceptor Kudi Gan as Grand Mentor, Minister of Works Peng Yue as Grand Marshal, Minister of Education Pan Xiangle as Minister of Works, Opening-Fu Third Rank Sima Ziru as Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin an edict appointed Grand Preceptor Kudi Gan as Grand Mentor, Minister of Works Peng Yue as Grand Marshal, Minister of Education Pan Xiangle as Minister of Works, and Opening-Fu Third Rank Sima Ziru as Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，以前太尉、清河王岳為使持節、驃騎大將軍、司州牧。

translations.literal: On xinmao, former Grand Marshal Prince of Qinghe Gao Yue was made Bearer of the Staff, Flying Cavalry Grand General, and Inspector of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao former Grand Marshal Prince of Qinghe Gao Yue was made Bearer of the Staff, Flying Cavalry Grand General, and Inspector of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，詔曰：「自今已後，諸有文啟論事並陳要密，有司悉為奏聞。

translations.literal: On renchen, an edict said: "From now on, all who have written memorials discussing affairs and stating essentials and secrets—the responsible offices shall all memorialize and report.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen an edict said: "From this day forward, all memorials discussing affairs and stating matters of importance or secrecy shall be forwarded and reported by the responsible offices.

sentences.zh: 」己亥，以皇太子初入東宮，赦畿內及并州死罪已下，餘州死降，徒流已下一皆原免。

translations.literal: On jihai, because the Crown Prince first entered the Eastern Palace, amnesty within the capital precincts and Bing Province for death crimes and below; in other provinces death reduced, exile and penal servitude and below all pardoned and exempted.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, because the crown prince first entered the Eastern Palace, death sentences and below were pardoned within the capital precincts and Bing Province; in other provinces death was commuted and exile and penal servitude and below were all remitted.

sentences.zh: 秋七月辛亥，詔尊文襄妃元氏為文襄皇后，宮曰靜德。
