translations.literal: From summer through the ninth month, great locust plagues struck the six provinces north of the Yellow River, the twelve provinces south of the Yellow River, and the eight commanderies of the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: From summer through the ninth month great locust plagues struck the six provinces north of the Yellow River, the twelve provinces south of it, and the eight commanderies of the capital region.

sentences.zh: 是月，飛至京師，蔽日，聲如風雨。

translations.literal: That month they flew as far as the capital, blotting out the sun, their sound like wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: That month they flew as far as the capital, blotting out the sun, with a sound like wind and rain.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，詔今年遭蝗之處免租。

translations.literal: On jiachen day, an edict remitted rent in all places struck by locusts that year.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day an edict remitted rent in every district struck by locusts that year.

sentences.zh: 是月，周冢宰宇文護殺其主閔帝而立帝弟毓，是為明帝。

translations.literal: That month Zhou's regent Yuwen Hu killed his ruler Emperor Min and enthroned the emperor's younger brother Yu, who became Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: That month Northern Zhou's regent Yuwen Hu killed his sovereign Emperor Min and enthroned the emperor's younger brother Yu, who became Emperor Ming.

sentences.zh: 冬十月乙亥，陳霸先弑其主方智自立，是為陳武帝，遣使稱藩朝貢。

translations.literal: On yihai day in the tenth month of winter, Chen Baxian murdered his ruler Fangzhi and enthroned himself, becoming Emperor Wu of Chen; he sent envoys declaring himself a vassal with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day in the tenth month of winter Chen Baxian murdered his sovereign Fangzhi and seized the throne as Emperor Wu of Chen, then sent envoys declaring vassalage and tribute.

sentences.zh: 是年，於長城內築重城，自庫洛拔而東至於塢紇戍，凡四百餘里。

translations.literal: That year, within the Great Wall a second wall was built from Kuluo Valley eastward to the Wuge Garrison, more than four hundred li in all.
translations.idiomatic: That year a second wall was built inside the Great Wall from Kuluo Valley eastward to Wuge Garrison, more than four hundred li in all.

sentences.zh: 九年春二月丁亥，降罪人。

translations.literal: In the second month of spring in the ninth year, on dinghai day, the sentences of convicts were reduced.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of spring of the ninth year, on dinghai day, the sentences of convicts were reduced.

sentences.zh: 己丑，詔限仲冬一月燎野，不得他時行火，損昆蟲草木。

translations.literal: On jichou day, an edict limited the burning of fields to the mid-winter month and forbade setting fires at other times, lest insects and vegetation be harmed.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou day an edict limited field-burning to the mid-winter month and forbade fires at other times, lest insects and plants be harmed.

sentences.zh: 三月丁酉，帝至自晉陽。

translations.literal: On dingyou day in the third month, the Emperor returned from Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day in the third month the emperor returned from Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 夏四月辛巳，大赦。

translations.literal: On xinsi day in the fourth month of summer, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day in the fourth month of summer a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 是夏，大旱。

translations.literal: That summer there was a great drought.
translations.idiomatic: That summer brought a great drought.

sentences.zh: 帝以祈雨不應，毀西門豹祠，掘其冢。

translations.literal: Because prayers for rain went unanswered, the Emperor destroyed the shrine of Ximen Bao and dug up his tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When prayers for rain went unanswered, the emperor destroyed the shrine of Ximen Bao and dug up his tomb.

sentences.zh: 山東大蝗，差夫役捕而坑之。

translations.literal: In Shandong there was a great locust plague; corvée laborers were dispatched to catch the insects and bury them in pits.
translations.idiomatic: In Shandong a great locust plague struck, and corvée laborers were sent to catch the insects and bury them in pits.

sentences.zh: 是月，北豫州刺史司馬消難以城叛，入於周。

translations.literal: That month Sima Xiaonan, governor of Northern Yuzhou, rebelled with his city and went over to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: That month Sima Xiaonan, governor of Northern Yuzhou, rebelled with his city and defected to Northern Zhou.

sentences.zh: 五月辛丑，尚書令、長廣王湛錄尚書事，驃騎大將軍、平秦王歸彥為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: On xinchou day in the fifth month, Prince Zhan of Changguang, Director of the Masters of Writing, was made recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Prince Guiyan of Pingqin, General of Agile Cavalry, was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day in the fifth month Prince Zhan of Changguang, director of the Masters of Writing, was made recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Prince Guiyan of Pingqin, general of agile cavalry, left vice director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，以前尚書左僕射楊愔為尚書令。

translations.literal: On jiachen day, former Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yang Yin was made Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day former left vice director of the Masters of Writing Yang Yin was made director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 六月乙丑，帝自晉陽北巡。

translations.literal: On yichou day in the sixth month, the Emperor toured north from Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou day in the sixth month the emperor set out on a northern tour from Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 己巳，至祁連池。

translations.literal: On jisi day he reached Qilian Pool.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi day he reached Qilian Pool.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，還晉陽。

translations.literal: On wuyin day he returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day he returned to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 秋七月辛丑，給京畿老人劉奴等九百四十三人版職及杖帽各有差。

translations.literal: On xinchou day in the seventh month of autumn, nine hundred forty-three elderly men of the capital region, including Liu Nu, were granted office tablets, canes, and caps in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day in the seventh month of autumn 943 elderly men of the capital region, including Liu Nu, were granted office tablets, canes, and caps in varying measure.

sentences.zh: 戊申，詔趙、燕、瀛、定、南營五州及司州廣平、清河二郡去年螽澇損田，兼春夏少雨，苗稼薄者，免今年租賦。

translations.literal: On wushen day, an edict remitted this year's rent and tax for fields damaged by locusts and floods last year in the five provinces of Zhao, Yan, Ying, Ding, and Southern Camp, and in the two commanderies of Guangping and Qinghe in Sizhou, as well as for fields whose crops were thin because spring and summer had brought little rain.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen day an edict remitted this year's rent and tax for fields in Zhao, Yan, Ying, Ding, and Southern Camp and in Guangping and Qinghe in Sizhou that had been damaged by locusts and floods the year before, and for fields whose crops were thin after a dry spring and summer.

sentences.zh: 八月乙丑，至自晉陽。

translations.literal: On yichou day in the eighth month, he returned from Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou day in the eighth month he returned from Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，帝如晉陽。

translations.literal: On jiaxu day, the Emperor went to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu day the emperor went to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 是月，陳江州刺史沈泰以三千人內附。

translations.literal: That month Shen Tai, governor of Jiangzhou in Chen, came over with three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: That month Shen Tai, Chen's governor of Jiangzhou, defected with three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 先是，發丁匠三十餘萬營三臺於鄴下，因其舊基而高博之，大起宮室及遊豫園。

translations.literal: Earlier, more than three hundred thousand corvée laborers and artisans had been mobilized to build the Three Towers below Ye on the old foundations, raising them higher and broader, and to construct great palaces and pleasure gardens.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier more than three hundred thousand corvée laborers and artisans had been mobilized to build the Three Towers below Ye on their old foundations, raising them higher and broader, and to erect great palaces and pleasure gardens.

sentences.zh: 至是，三臺成，改銅爵曰金鳳，金獸曰聖應，冰井曰崇光。

translations.literal: By this time the Three Towers were complete; Copper Sparrow was renamed Golden Phoenix, Golden Beast was renamed Holy Response, and Ice Well was renamed Glorious Light.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Three Towers were finished: Copper Sparrow was renamed Golden Phoenix, Golden Beast Holy Response, and Ice Well Glorious Light.

sentences.zh: 十一月甲午，帝至自晉陽，登三臺，御乾象殿，朝讌群臣，並命賦詩。

translations.literal: On jiawu day in the eleventh month, the Emperor returned from Jinyang, ascended the Three Towers, presided in the Qianxiang Hall, held court and feasted the hundred officials, and ordered them all to compose poems.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day in the eleventh month the emperor returned from Jinyang, ascended the Three Towers, presided in Qianxiang Hall, held court and feasted the hundred officials, and ordered them all to compose poems.

sentences.zh: 以新宮成，丁酉，大赦，內外文武普汎一大階。

translations.literal: Because the new palace was complete, on dingyou day a general amnesty was proclaimed, and civil and military officials within and without were universally promoted one full rank.
translations.idiomatic: With the new palace complete, on dingyou day a general amnesty was proclaimed and every civil and military official within and without the court was promoted one full rank.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，梁湘州刺史王琳遣使請立蕭莊為梁主，仍以江州內屬，令莊居之。

translations.literal: On dingsi day, Wang Lin, governor of Xiangzhou in Liang, sent envoys asking that Xiao Zhuang be established as ruler of Liang, with Jiangzhou submitted to Qi and Zhuang installed there.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi day Wang Lin, Liang's governor of Xiangzhou, sent envoys asking that Xiao Zhuang be established as ruler of Liang, with Jiangzhou submitted to Qi and Zhuang installed there.

sentences.zh: 十二月癸酉，詔梁王蕭莊為梁主，進居九派。

translations.literal: On guiyou day in the twelfth month, an edict established Xiao Zhuang as ruler of Liang and had him advance to Jiupai.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou day in the twelfth month an edict established Xiao Zhuang as ruler of Liang and had him advance to Jiupai.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，乙太傅可朱渾道元為太師，司徒尉粲為太尉，冀州刺史段韶為司空，錄尚書事、常山王演為大司馬，錄尚書事、長廣王湛為司徒。

translations.literal: On wuyin day, Grand Tutor Kezhuhun Daoyuan was promoted to Grand Preceptor; Minister over the Masses Wei Can was made Grand Commandant; Duan Shao, governor of Jizhou, was made Minister of Works; Prince Yan of Changshan, recorder of the Masters of Writing, was made Grand Marshal; and Prince Zhan of Changguang, recorder of the Masters of Writing, was made Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day Grand Tutor Kezhuhun Daoyuan was promoted to grand preceptor; Minister over the Masses Wei Can, grand commandant; Duan Shao, governor of Jizhou, minister of works; Prince Yan of Changshan, recorder of the Masters of Writing, grand marshal; and Prince Zhan of Changguang, recorder of the Masters of Writing, minister over the masses.

sentences.zh: 是月，起大莊嚴寺。

translations.literal: That month construction began on the Great Solemnity Temple.
translations.idiomatic: That month construction began on the Great Solemnity Temple.

sentences.zh: 是年，殺永安王浚、上黨王渙。

translations.literal: That year Prince Jun of Yong'an and Prince Huan of Shangdang were killed.
translations.idiomatic: That year Prince Jun of Yong'an and Prince Huan of Shangdang were put to death.

sentences.zh: 十年春正月戊戌，以司空侯莫陳相為大將軍。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the tenth year, on wuxu day, Houmochen Xiang, Minister of Works, was made Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring of the tenth year, on wuxu day, Minister of Works Houmochen Xiang was made grand general.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，帝如遼陽甘露寺。

translations.literal: On jiayin day, the Emperor went to the Sweet Dew Temple at Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day the emperor went to Sweet Dew Temple at Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，詔於麻城置衡州。

translations.literal: On yimao day, an edict established Hengzhou at Macheng.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day an edict established Hengzhou at Macheng.

sentences.zh: 二月丙戌，帝於甘露寺禪居深觀，唯軍國大政奏聞。

translations.literal: On bingxu day in the second month, the Emperor took up Chan retreat at Sweet Dew Temple in deep contemplation; only great affairs of state and the army were reported to him.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu day in the second month the emperor withdrew to Sweet Dew Temple for Chan retreat and deep contemplation; only great affairs of state and the army were reported to him.

sentences.zh: 三月戊戌，以侍中高德政為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: On wuxu day in the third month, Palace Attendant Gao Dezheng was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu day in the third month Palace Attendant Gao Dezheng was made right vice director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，帝至自遼陽。

translations.literal: On bingchen day, the Emperor returned from Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen day the emperor returned from Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 是月，梁主蕭莊至郢州，遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: That month the Liang ruler Xiao Zhuang reached Yingzhou and sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Liang ruler Xiao Zhuang reached Yingzhou and sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 閏四月丁酉，以司州牧、彭城王浟為司空，侍中、高陽王湜為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fourth month, on dingyou day, Prince You of Pengcheng, governor of Sizhou, was made Minister of Works, and Palace Attendant Prince Shi of Gaoyang was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fourth month, on dingyou day, Prince You of Pengcheng, governor of Sizhou, was made minister of works, and Palace Attendant Prince Shi of Gaoyang, right vice director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，以司空、彭城王浟兼太尉，封皇子紹廉為長樂郡王。

translations.literal: On yisi day, Prince You of Pengcheng, Minister of Works, was additionally made Grand Commandant, and the emperor's son Shaoqian was enfeoffed as Prince of Changle Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day Prince You of Pengcheng, minister of works, was additionally made grand commandant, and the emperor's son Shaoqian was enfeoffed as Prince of Changle Commandery.

sentences.zh: 五月癸未，誅始平西元世、東平西元景式等二十五家，特進元韶等十九家並令禁止。

translations.literal: On guiwei day in the fifth month, twenty-five households of the Yuan clan, including Shixi of the Western Capital and Jingshi of the Eastern Capital, were executed, and nineteen households including Special Advance Yuan Shao were placed under restriction.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day in the fifth month twenty-five households of the Yuan clan, including Shixi of the Western Capital and Jingshi of the Eastern Capital, were executed, and nineteen households including Special Advance Yuan Shao were placed under restriction.

sentences.zh: 六月，陳武帝殂，兄子蒨立，是為文帝。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Emperor Wu of Chen died; his elder brother's son Qian succeeded him, becoming Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Emperor Wu of Chen died; his elder brother's son Qian succeeded him as Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 秋八月戊戌，封皇子紹義為廣陽郡王，以尚書右僕射、河間王孝琬為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: On wuxu day in the eighth month of autumn, the emperor's son Shaoyi was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangyang Commandery, and Prince Xiaowan of Hejian, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was made Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu day in the eighth month of autumn the emperor's son Shaoyi was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangyang Commandery, and Prince Xiaowan of Hejian, right vice director of the Masters of Writing, was made left vice director.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，詔諸軍民或有父祖改姓冒入元氏，或假託攜認，忘稱姓元者，不問世數遠近，悉聽改復本姓。

translations.literal: On guimao day, an edict ordered that among soldiers and commoners any who had changed their surname to enter the Yuan clan by fraud, or who falsely claimed kinship and forgot to declare their original surname because they called themselves Yuan, regardless of how many generations had passed, were all permitted to restore their original surname.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao day an edict ordered that soldiers and commoners who had changed their surname to pass as Yuan, or who falsely claimed kinship and forgot their original surname because they called themselves Yuan, were all permitted to restore their original surname, no matter how many generations had passed.

sentences.zh: 九月己巳，帝如晉陽。

translations.literal: On jisi day in the ninth month, the Emperor went to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi day in the ninth month the emperor went to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 是月，使酈懷則、陸仁惠使於蕭莊。

translations.literal: That month Li Huai'ze and Lu Renhui were sent as envoys to Xiao Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: That month Li Huai'ze and Lu Renhui were dispatched as envoys to Xiao Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 冬十月甲午，帝暴崩於晉陽宮德陽堂，時年三十一。

translations.literal: On jiawu day in the tenth month of winter, the Emperor suddenly died in the Deyang Hall of Jinyang Palace; he was thirty-one.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day in the tenth month of winter the emperor suddenly died in Deyang Hall of Jinyang Palace; he was thirty-one.

sentences.zh: 遺詔：「凡諸凶事一依儉約。

translations.literal: The testamentary edict read: "All affairs of mourning shall follow austerity in every respect.
translations.idiomatic: The testamentary edict read: "All affairs of mourning shall follow austerity in every respect.

sentences.zh: 三年之喪，雖曰達禮，漢文革創，通行自昔，義有存焉，同之可也，喪月之斷限以三十六日。

translations.literal: The three-year mourning, though called the fulfillment of ritual, had since Han emperor Wen's reign been curtailed and practiced from of old; its spirit still had standing and might be adopted alike, with the period of mourning fixed at thirty-six days.
translations.idiomatic: The three-year mourning, though called the fulfillment of ritual, had since Emperor Wen of Han curtailed it and the practice had continued from of old; its spirit still stood and might be adopted alike, with mourning fixed at thirty-six days.

sentences.zh: 嗣主、百僚、內外遐邇奉制割情，悉從公除。

translations.literal: The heir, the hundred officials, and all near and far, domestic and foreign, were to set aside private grief in obedience to the edict and observe public mourning throughout.
translations.idiomatic: The heir, the hundred officials, and all near and far, at home and abroad, were to set aside private grief in obedience to the edict and observe public mourning throughout.

sentences.zh: 」癸卯，發喪，斂於宣德殿。

translations.literal: " On guimao day mourning was announced and the body was laid out in Xuande Hall.
translations.idiomatic: " On guimao day mourning was announced and the body was laid out in Xuande Hall.

sentences.zh: 十一月辛未，梓宮還京師。

translations.literal: On xinwei day in the eleventh month, the coffin returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei day in the eleventh month the coffin returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十二月乙酉，殯於太極前殿。

translations.literal: On yiyou day in the twelfth month, the body was interred in the hall before the Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou day in the twelfth month the body was placed in the hall before the Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 乾明元年二月丙申，葬于武寧陵，諡曰文宣皇帝，廟號威宗。

translations.literal: On bingchen day in the second month of the first year of Ganming, he was buried at Wuning Tomb, posthumously titled Emperor Wenxuan, with the temple name Weizong.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen day in the second month of the first year of Ganming he was buried at Wuning Tomb, posthumously titled Emperor Wenxuan, with the temple name Weizong.

sentences.zh: 武平初，又改為文宣，廟號顯祖。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Wuping era, the title was again changed to Wenxuan and the temple name to Xianzu.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wuping era the title was again changed to Wenxuan and the temple name to Xianzu.

sentences.zh: 帝少有大度，志識沉敏，外柔內剛，果敢能斷。

translations.literal: From youth the Emperor had great breadth of mind; his purpose and understanding were deep and keen; outwardly gentle, inwardly firm; bold and resolute in decision.
translations.idiomatic: From youth the emperor had great breadth of mind; his purpose and understanding were deep and keen; outwardly gentle yet inwardly firm; bold and resolute in judgment.

sentences.zh: 雅好吏事，測始知終，理劇處繁，終日不倦。

translations.literal: He was fond of administrative affairs by nature; measuring from beginning to end, he handled difficult and complex matters all day without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he loved administrative work; tracing matters from beginning to end, he handled the most difficult and complex affairs all day without weariness.

sentences.zh: 初踐大位，留心政術，以法馭下，公道為先。

translations.literal: When he first ascended the throne, he gave his heart to statecraft, governing subordinates by law and putting fairness first.
translations.idiomatic: When he first ascended the throne he gave his heart to statecraft, governing subordinates by law and putting fairness first.

sentences.zh: 或有違犯憲章，雖密戚舊勳，必無容舍，內外清靖，莫不祗肅。

translations.literal: If anyone violated the statutes, even close kin or old merit-holders were shown no indulgence; within and without the court all was clear and quiet, and none failed to stand in reverent awe.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone violated the statutes, even close kin or old merit-holders were shown no indulgence; within and without the court all was clear and quiet, and none failed to stand in reverent awe.

sentences.zh: 至於軍國幾策，獨決懷抱，規模巨集遠，有人君大略。

translations.literal: As for military and state strategy, he decided alone in his breast; his designs were vast and far-reaching, and he had the great outline of a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: In military and state strategy he decided alone in his breast; his designs were vast and far-reaching, and he had the great outline of a true sovereign.

sentences.zh: 又以三方鼎跱，諸夷未賓，修繕甲兵，簡練士卒，左右宿衛置百保軍士。

translations.literal: Because the three realms stood like tripods and the various tribes had not yet submitted, he repaired armor and weapons, drilled and selected soldiers, and stationed a hundred-company guard force among his personal attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Because the three realms stood like tripods and the various tribes had not yet submitted, he repaired armor and weapons, drilled and selected soldiers, and stationed a hundred-company guard force among his personal attendants.

sentences.zh: 每臨行陣，親當矢石，鋒刃交接，唯恐前敵之不多，屢犯艱危，常致克捷。

translations.literal: Whenever he went to the battle line he personally faced arrows and stones; when blades crossed he feared only that the enemy in front were too few, and repeatedly braved hardship and danger, often achieving victory.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he went to the battle line he personally faced arrows and stones; when blades crossed he feared only that the enemy before him were too few, and repeatedly braved hardship and danger, often achieving victory.

sentences.zh: 嘗于東山遊讌，以關隴未平，投杯震怒，召魏收於御前，立為詔書，宣示遠近，將事西伐。

translations.literal: Once, while feasting on the Eastern Hill, because Guanlong was not yet pacified he threw down his cup in rage, summoned Wei Shou before him, and had an edict drafted on the spot to proclaim to far and near that he would campaign west.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while feasting on the Eastern Hill, because Guanlong was not yet pacified he threw down his cup in rage, summoned Wei Shou before him, and had an edict drafted on the spot proclaiming to far and near that he would campaign west.

sentences.zh: 是歲，周文帝殂，西人震恐，常為度隴之計。

translations.literal: That year Emperor Wen of Zhou died; the people of the west were shaken with fear, and plans to cross Long were often made.
translations.idiomatic: That year Emperor Wen of Northern Zhou died; the people of the west were shaken with fear, and plans to cross Long were often made.

sentences.zh: 既征伐四克，威振戎夏，六七年後，以功業自矜，遂留連耽湎，肆行淫暴。

translations.literal: After his campaigns conquered on four fronts and his might shook the barbarians and the Chinese, six or seven years later he grew proud of his achievements, lingered in dissipation, and indulged in lewdness and violence.
translations.idiomatic: After his campaigns conquered on four fronts and his might shook barbarians and Chinese alike, six or seven years later he grew proud of his achievements, lingered in dissipation, and indulged in lewdness and violence.

sentences.zh: 或躬自鼓舞，歌謳不息，從旦通宵，以夜繼晝。

translations.literal: Sometimes he danced and sang himself without cease, from dawn through the night and on through the day.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he danced and sang himself without cease, from dawn through the night and on through the day.

sentences.zh: 或袒露形體，塗傅粉黛，散發胡服，雜衣錦彩。

translations.literal: Sometimes he bared his body, smeared on powder and rouge, let his hair hang loose in barbarian dress, and wore mixed garments of brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he bared his body, smeared on powder and rouge, let his hair hang loose in barbarian dress, and wore mixed garments of brocade.

sentences.zh: 拔刃張弓，游於市肆，勳戚之第，朝夕臨幸。

translations.literal: Drawing blade and bow, he roamed the markets and visited the mansions of meritorious kin morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Blade drawn and bow in hand, he roamed the markets and visited the mansions of meritorious kin morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 時乘馲駝牛驢，不施鞍勒，盛暑炎赫，隆冬酷寒，或日中暴身，去衣馳騁，從者不堪，帝居之自若。

translations.literal: At times he rode camels, mules, oxen, and donkeys without saddle or bridle; in fierce summer heat or bitter winter cold, or baring himself at midday and riding stripped, his attendants could not endure it, yet the Emperor was entirely at ease.
translations.idiomatic: At times he rode camels, mules, oxen, and donkeys without saddle or bridle; in fierce summer heat or bitter winter cold, or baring himself at midday and riding stripped, his attendants could not endure it, yet the emperor was entirely at ease.

sentences.zh: 親戚貴臣，左右近習，侍從錯雜，無復差等。

translations.literal: Relatives of merit, honored ministers, and close attendants were mixed together in his company without any distinction of rank.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives of merit, honored ministers, and close attendants were mixed together in his company without any distinction of rank.

sentences.zh: 徵集淫嫗，分付從官，朝夕臨視，以為娛樂。

translations.literal: He summoned licentious women and assigned them to his attendants, visiting them morning and evening for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned licentious women and assigned them to his attendants, visiting them morning and evening for amusement.

sentences.zh: 凡諸殺害，多令支解，或焚之於火，或投之於河。

translations.literal: Of all the killings, many were ordered dismembered, or burned in fire, or cast into rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Of all the killings, many were ordered dismembered, burned in fire, or cast into rivers.

sentences.zh: 沉酗既久，彌以狂惑，至於末年，每言見諸鬼物，亦云聞異音聲。

translations.literal: Deep drunkenness lasting long made him ever more frenzied and deluded; in his final years he constantly said he saw ghosts, and also that he heard strange sounds.
translations.idiomatic: Deep drunkenness lasting long made him ever more frenzied and deluded; in his final years he constantly said he saw ghosts and heard strange sounds.

sentences.zh: 情有蒂芥，必在誅戮，諸元宗室咸加屠剿，永安、上黨並致冤酷，高隆之、高德政、杜弼、王元景、李蒨之等皆以非罪加害。

translations.literal: If resentment took root in his heart, execution was inevitable; the Yuan of the imperial clan were all slaughtered, and Prince Jun of Yong'an and Prince Huan of Shangdang met cruel injustice; Gao Longzhi, Gao Dezheng, Du Bi, Wang Yuanjing, Li Qianzhi, and others were all harmed on false charges.
translations.idiomatic: If resentment took root in his heart, execution was inevitable; the Yuan of the imperial clan were slaughtered wholesale, and Prince Jun of Yong'an and Prince Huan of Shangdang met cruel injustice; Gao Longzhi, Gao Dezheng, Du Bi, Wang Yuanjing, Li Qianzhi, and others were all destroyed on false charges.

sentences.zh: 嘗在晉陽以槊戲刺都督尉子耀，應手即殞。

translations.literal: Once at Jinyang he playfully stabbed Supervisor Wei Ziyao with a spear, and Wei fell dead at once.
translations.idiomatic: Once at Jinyang he playfully stabbed Supervisor Wei Ziyao with a spear, and Wei fell dead at once.

sentences.zh: 又在三臺大光殿上，以鋸鋸都督穆嵩，遂至於死。

translations.literal: Again, on the Great Light Hall of the Three Towers he sawed Supervisor Mu Song with a saw until he died.
translations.idiomatic: Again, in Great Light Hall of the Three Towers he sawed Supervisor Mu Song with a saw until he died.

sentences.zh: 又嘗幸開府暴顯家，有都督韓悊無罪，忽於衆中喚出斬之。

translations.literal: Again, while visiting the residence of Kaifu Bao Xian, he called out Supervisor Han Ti, who was innocent, from among the crowd and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Again, while visiting the residence of Kaifu Bao Xian, he called out the innocent Supervisor Han Ti from among the crowd and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 自餘酷濫，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: The rest of the cruel excess was beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The rest of the cruel excess was beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 朝野憯憎，各懷怨毒。

translations.literal: Court and countryside were filled with anguish; each nursed resentment and hatred.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside were filled with anguish; each nursed resentment and hatred.

sentences.zh: 而素以嚴斷臨下，加之默識強記，百僚戰慄，不敢為非，文武近臣，朝不謀夕。

translations.literal: Yet because he had always governed subordinates with stern decisiveness, and moreover possessed a silent memory of great strength, the hundred officials trembled with fear and dared not do wrong; civil and military close attendants did not know whether they would live to see the morrow.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because he had always governed subordinates with stern decisiveness, and moreover possessed a silent memory of great strength, the hundred officials trembled with fear and dared not do wrong; civil and military close attendants did not know whether they would live to see the morrow.

sentences.zh: 又多所營繕，百役繁興，舉國騷擾，公私勞弊。

translations.literal: He also undertook many constructions; corvée labor multiplied throughout the realm, the whole state was thrown into turmoil, and public and private alike were worn out with toil.
translations.idiomatic: He also undertook many constructions; corvée labor multiplied throughout the realm, the whole state was thrown into turmoil, and public and private alike were worn out with toil.

sentences.zh: 凡諸賞賚，無復節限，府藏之積，遂至空虛。

translations.literal: As for all rewards and bestowals, there were no longer any limits; the accumulations of the treasury were eventually emptied.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards and bestowals knew no limit, and the treasury's stores were drained empty.

sentences.zh: 自皇太后諸王及內外勳舊，愁懼危悚，計無所出。

translations.literal: From the Empress Dowager and the princes to meritorious elders within and without the court, all were anxious, fearful, and peril-stricken, with no plan to escape.
translations.idiomatic: From the Empress Dowager and the princes to meritorious elders within and without the court, all lived in dread and peril, with nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 暨于末年，不能進食，唯數飲酒，麴蘖成災，因而致斃。

translations.literal: By his final years he could no longer take food and drank wine only; fermented malt became a calamity, and so he died.
translations.idiomatic: In his final years he could no longer eat and drank only wine; fermented malt became his ruin, and he died of it.

sentences.zh: 論曰：高祖平定四胡，威權延世。

translations.literal: Commentary: The Grand Ancestor pacified the four barbarian peoples, and his authority endured for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The Grand Ancestor pacified the four barbarian peoples, and his authority endured for generations.

sentences.zh: 遷鄴之後，雖主器有人，號令所加，政皆自出。

translations.literal: After the move to Ye, though the heir's vessel was held by another, every command issued and every policy came from himself.
translations.idiomatic: After the move to Ye, though an heir held the vessel of state, every command and every policy still issued from the regent alone.

sentences.zh: 顯祖因循鴻業，內外協從，自朝及野，群心屬望。

translations.literal: The Founding Ancestor inherited the great enterprise; inner and outer aligned in obedience, from court to countryside all hearts looked to him.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Ancestor inherited the great enterprise; court and countryside alike fell into step, and every heart turned toward him.

sentences.zh: 東魏之地，舉世樂推，曾未期月，玄運集己。

translations.literal: Throughout the lands of Eastern Wei all gladly urged him forward; not even a full month had passed before the dark mandate gathered upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout Eastern Wei all gladly urged him forward; before a month had passed the dark mandate had gathered upon him.

sentences.zh: 始則存心政事，風化肅然，數年之間，翕斯致治。

translations.literal: At first he applied his mind to government; customs grew solemn and upright, and within a few years he brought order together.
translations.idiomatic: At first he gave his mind to government; customs grew solemn and upright, and within a few years he had brought the realm to order.

sentences.zh: 其後縱酒肆欲，事極倡狂，昏邪殘暴，近世未有。

translations.literal: Afterward he gave free rein to wine and desire, indulging to the utmost in madness; his delusion, wickedness, cruelty, and ferocity were unmatched in recent ages.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he gave free rein to wine and desire, indulging madness to the limit; his delusion, wickedness, cruelty, and ferocity were unmatched in recent memory.

sentences.zh: 饗國弗永，實由斯疾，胤嗣殄絕，固亦餘殃者也。

translations.literal: That he did not long enjoy the realm was truly due to this malady; the extinction of his heirs was likewise the lingering curse of it.
translations.idiomatic: That he did not long enjoy the realm was truly due to this sickness; the extinction of his line was likewise the lingering curse of it.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：天保定位，受終攸屬。

translations.literal: Appraisal: In the Tianbao reign the throne was fixed; to receive the end of the mandate was his allotted portion.
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal: In the Tianbao reign the throne was fixed; to receive the mandate's end was his allotted portion.

sentences.zh: 奄宅區夏，爰膺帝籙。

translations.literal: He took possession of the central lands and thereupon received the imperial tally.
translations.idiomatic: He took possession of the central lands and thereupon received the imperial tally.

sentences.zh: 勢叶謳歌，情毀龜玉。

translations.literal: The momentum matched the people's song of praise; yet the sentiment later ruined the jade tally and regalia.
translations.idiomatic: The momentum matched the people's song of praise; yet in the end his heart ruined the jade tally and regalia.

sentences.zh: 始存政術，聞斯德音。

translations.literal: At first he preserved the art of government, and men heard his virtuous words.
translations.idiomatic: At first he preserved the art of government, and men heard his virtuous words.

sentences.zh: 罔遵克念，乃肆其心。

translations.literal: He did not keep to self-restraint and so gave his heart full license.
translations.idiomatic: He did not keep to self-restraint and gave his heart full license.

sentences.zh: 窮理殘虐，盡性荒淫。

translations.literal: He pushed reason to cruelty and indulgence to the utmost in debauchery.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed reason to cruelty and indulgence to the utmost in debauchery.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年十一月、第一版《北齊書》為本校。

translations.literal: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi, November 1972, as the base for collation.
translations.idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972).
